items.summary: Universally Baire sets are a standard tool in modern set theory, where they are closely connected with forcing and absoluteness. In this paper we study universal Baireness instead as purely a regularity notion for subsets of Polish spaces. Our aim is not to develop the set-theoretic theory, but to place the notion on a systematic descriptive-set-theoretic footing and to clarify the several nonequivalent definitions that occur in the literature. A subset of a Polish space is called \emph{universally Baire} if all its continuous preimages possess the property of Baire. However, it is important to specify what the domain of these continuous functions can be. In fact, a plethora of definitions are used by various authors in the literature, the class of possible domains is sometimes the class of Polish spaces, compact metrizable spaces, all topological spaces, compact topological spaces, etc. We clarify this situation by demonstrating that the above four options are pairwise nonequivalent under the Continuum Hypothesis, we determine all the implications between these four notions that are provable in $ZFC$, and also show that all the notions used in the literature are equivalent to one of these four. Furthermore, we use Miller forcing to show that actually the cases of Polish and compact metrizable spaces are consistently equivalent. We show that numerous definitions using Borel isomorphisms, changes of topologies and Boolean algebras are all equivalent to the case of Polish domains. We present an argument that the notion using Polish domains is the natural dual to the notion of universally measurable sets. Finally, as a byproduct, we prove that the following statement is independent of $ZFC$: if a subset of a Polish space has the property of Baire relative to every nowhere dense Cantor subspace, then the subset has the property of Baire in the whole space.

items.title: The complexity of smooth words over binary alphabets
items.summary: Smooth sequences over an alphabet of positive integers $\{a,b\}$ are sequences that are infinitely derivable, the emblematic example being the Oldenburger-Kolakoski sequence $κ$ over $\{1,2\}$. The main way to study their language is to consider a finite version of smooth sequences called smooth words. In this paper we prove that the smooth words are exactly the factors of smooth sequences and we make progress towards the conjecture that the complexity of smooth words over $\{a,b\}$ grows like $Θ\left(n^{\log(a+b)/\log((a+b)/2)}\right)$: we prove the lower bound over any alphabet and the upper bound over even alphabets, and we improve the known upper bound over odd and mixed alphabets. We also provide a dichotomy that links the language, the morphicity and the factor complexity of $κ$.

items.title: A convolution inequality and the Krzyż conjecture
items.summary: Using a sharp bound for convolutions of non-negative trigonometric polynomials with the Fejér kernel resembling a pointwise variant of Bernstein's inequality for polynomials, we prove new properties of extremal functions for the Krzyż conjecture. In particular, we resolve a 1993 conjecture of Peretz by showing that if $f$ is extremal for some coefficient, then $|f(0)|\leq 1/e$. Furthermore, we show that if equality holds in this estimate for every extremal function, then the Krzyż conjecture is true.

items.title: Overholonomicity of Overconvergent $F$-isocrystals over Laurent Series Fields
items.summary: We prove that $K$-valued overconvergent $F$-isocrystals over smooth $k((t))$-varieties are overholonomic and construct the triangulated category of overholonomic complexes of Frobenius type which is stable under six operations and contains overconvergent $F$-isocrsytals.

items.title: Thermodynamic formalism for non-compact systems with expansivity and specification
items.summary: We develop a new theory of thermodynamic formalism for non-compact flows, providing criteria for existence and uniqueness of equilibrium states, as well as ergodicity and a Gibbs property. These criteria include new versions of the expansivity and specification properties that hold for geodesic flows on non-compact negatively curved manifolds. Previous results on thermodynamic formalism for these geodesic flows were restricted by a pinched curvature condition, which we remove, allowing curvature to approach both $0$ and $-\infty$. Our results also apply to geodesic flows beyond the smooth setting, including locally CAT(-1) spaces.

items.title: An interpretation of the BMO boundedness of Hörmander--Mikhlin multipliers
items.summary: We prove a pointwise domination of Poisson variances for Hörmander--Mikhlin multipliers on the real line. The estimate holds in operator order for operator-valued functions and gives a direct Fourier-side proof of BMO boundedness. The same argument gives an algebraic proof of the one-dimensional Schur multiplier estimate of Conde-Alonso, González-Pérez, Parcet and Tablate ( Annals of Mathematics, 2023), formulated here using Poisson BMO. The endpoint estimates are proved for $L^2$ functions and Hilbert--Schmidt operators; interpolation gives the corresponding $L^p$ and Schatten estimates.

items.title: Torsion points in families of elliptic curves
items.summary: We study the specialization of torsion points in one-parameter degenerations of elliptic curves with singular fibers of Kodaira type. We describe the resulting torsion curves, their ramifications, intersection multiplicities, and irreducible and connected components.

items.title: Failure of Pólya-Szegő inequality for weighted nonlocal seminorm and on nonlocal C-K-N inequality
items.summary: We create counterexamples to show that Pólya-Szegő type of inequality fails for the weighted nonlocal seminorm \begin{equation*} [u]_{W^{s,p, α}(\mathbb{R}^d)} := \left( \int_{\mathbb{R}^d} \int_{\mathbb{R}^d} \frac{|x|^{α_{1} p} |y|^{α_{2} p} |u(x)-u(y)|^{p}}{|x-y|^{d+sp}} \, dx \, dy \right)^{\frac{1}{p}} \ , \end{equation*} in all three regimes $α_1 +α_2 < 0, \, α_1 +α_2 = 0$, and $α_1 +α_2 >0$. These counterexamples are such that it completely settles the first two cases for all parameters. We also provide necessary and sufficient conditions on the parameters for $ [u]_{W^{s,p, α}(\mathbb{R}^d)} < \infty$, thus extending an earlier known result of [Serena Dipierro and Enrico Valdinoci, A density property for fractional weighted Sobolev spaces]. We also provide another proof of the fractional C-K-N type inequality, for most of the parameters (Hardy and Sobolev are included), using a familiar technique which is involved in the proof of fractional Sobolev inequality of [Eleonora Di Nezza, Giampiero Palatucci, and Enrico Valdinoci, Hitchhiker's guide to the fractional Sobolev spaces, Bulletin des sciences mathematiques] together with a symmetrization technique.

items.title: On generalized token graphs with tokens of different colors
items.summary: We generalize the concept of token graphs, and we call them supertoken graphs. In this work, we consider the variant in which tokens are distinguishable (for instance, by color) and at most one token is allowed on each vertex. We formally define this kind of supertoken graphs and present their basic properties. We study their diameter, in which cases they are Cayley graphs, and their spectra. Moreover, we provide bounds or exact values for the independence, the vertex cover, the clique, and the chromatic numbers of these graphs. Finally, we characterize the cases in which the supertoken graphs of complete graphs are planar.

items.title: Uniqueness of the critical and supercritical Liouville quantum gravity metrics
items.summary: We show that for each ${\mathbf c}_{\mathrm M} \in [1,25)$, there is a unique metric associated with Liouville quantum gravity (LQG) with matter central charge ${\mathbf c}_{\mathrm M}$. An earlier series of works by Ding-Dubédat-Dunlap-Falconet, Gwynne-Miller, and others showed that such a metric exists and is unique in the subcritical case ${\mathbf c}_{\mathrm M} \in (-\infty,1)$, which corresponds to coupling constant $γ\in (0,2)$. The critical case ${\mathbf c}_{\mathrm M} = 1$ corresponds to $γ=2$ and the supercritical case ${\mathbf c}_{\mathrm M} \in (1,25)$ corresponds to $γ\in \mathbb C$ with $|γ| = 2$. Our metric is constructed as the limit of an approximation procedure called Liouville first passage percolation, which was previously shown to be tight for $\mathbf c_{\mathrm M} \in [1,25)$ by Ding and Gwynne (2020). In this paper, we show that the subsequential limit is uniquely characterized by a natural list of axioms. This extends the characterization of the LQG metric proven by Gwynne and Miller (2019) for $\mathbf c_{\mathrm M} \in (-\infty,1)$ to the full parameter range $\mathbf c_{\mathrm M} \in (-\infty,25)$. Our argument is substantially different from the proof of the characterization of the LQG metric for $\mathbf c_{\mathrm M} \in (-\infty,1)$. In particular, the core part of the argument is simpler and does not use confluence of geodesics.

items.title: Gradient potential estimates for k-Hessian equations
items.summary: For $2\le k<n$, we prove pointwise gradient bounds for proper weak $k$-convex functions in terms of a local average and a Wolff potential of the full Hessian measure $F_k[u]$. The estimate yields local Lipschitz regularity for $F_k[u]=f$ with $f\in L^{n/k,1/k}_{\mathrm{loc}}$, and for $F_k[u]=|Du|^p$ when $0<p<nk/(n-k)$. Both the Lorentz index $1/k$ and the upper bound on $p$ are sharp.

items.title: Gaussian Matrices and Exterior Forms: Deterministic Principal Ideals
items.summary: For an infinite Gaussian matrix with independent entries and doubly monotone variances, we identify its algebraic principal ideal by a deterministic shell profile. The exact boundedness condition also implies compactness. A lower singular-value estimate uniform in the mean gives an exact sum law under each fixed compact perturbation. Conditional products and spatial compression yield the corresponding classification for Gaussian evaluations of Hilbert two-forms. For Wiener area of covariance rank at least two, the generator is the covariance tail divided by its index. The area and covariance generate the same ideal precisely under regularity at infinity.

items.title: Hopf algebra polynomial identities in the Sweedler algebra
items.summary: Using Mac Lane's PROPs, one can introduce multilinear polynomial identities that involve all the operations of a Hopf algebra: the (co)multiplication, the (co)unit and the antipode. We find bases for polynomial identities and calculate their codimensions for the Sweedler algebra, treating it first as an ordinary associative algebra over a field and second as a Hopf algebra.

items.title: Quantitative Tiling Stability From Quadratic Discrepancy In Hamming Spaces
items.summary: Quadratic ball discrepancy measures how uniformly a code meets Hamming balls over all centers and radii. Perfect codes minimize this quantity among codes of the same cardinality. We prove a quantitative refinement: at the parameters of every perfect code other than a one-word code or the full space, the discrepancy excess over the minimum is at least an explicit positive multiple of the discrepancy at the packing radius. The latter equals the tiling defect divided by the square of the code cardinality. This defect is the total squared deviation of the covering multiplicity from one. The comparison applies to all codes of that cardinality. For one-error perfect codes, the coefficient is at least one, and no larger constant holds for all such codes; explicit coefficients depending on the parameters can be much larger. The tiling defect also measures the failure of uniform ball noise to smooth a code distribution. Consequently, the same discrepancy excess gives explicit bounds on holes, overlaps, and divergence from the uniform distribution.

items.title: Universal Dimension Formula for Planar $C^r$ Splines at Degree $3r+1$
items.summary: We prove that Schumaker's lower bound gives the dimension of $S_{3r+1}^r(Δ)$ for every nondegenerate triangulation $Δ$ of a polygonal disk in $\mathbb{R}^2$ and every integer $r\ge3$. After accounting for the local vertex contributions, we reduce the remaining dimension defect to compatible vertex functionals. Apolarity associates a unique polynomial with each face, and compatibility forces differences of adjacent face polynomials to contain powers of both endpoint forms. We eliminate the leading residual coefficient using Hermite relations when $r$ is odd and an additional coefficient comparison when $r$ is even. A uniform induction then raises the endpoint powers until all face differences vanish; the zero boundary face potentials imply that every vertex functional vanishes and the global defect is zero. Together with the known cases $r=1,2$ and Hong's higher-degree theorem, this yields the dimension formula for all $r\ge1$ and $d\ge3r+1$.

items.title: Langevin Monte-Carlo Provably Learns Depth Two Neural Nets at Any Size and Data
items.summary: In this note we prove that the Langevin Monte Carlo (LMC) algorithm can minimize the population risk of appropriately regularized depth-2 nets with no restrictions on the size of the net and for any choice of training data --- and we give non-asymptotic convergence rates for it. We achieve this via showing that in q-Renyi divergence, the iterates of LMC converge to the Gibbs distribution of certain Frobenius norm regularized losses for these nets --- in both classification and regression settings. The key technicality of the work is two-fold (a) to keep the amount of regularization needed be independent of the size of the net and (b) to obtain convergence rates that scale with just the Poincare constant of the corresponding Gibbs measure. This work synthesizes several recent observations about isoperimetry conditions under which LMC converges and that two-layer neural loss functions can always be regularized by a constant amount such that they satisfy the Villani conditions, and thus their Gibbs measures satisfy a Poincare inequality.

items.title: Semistable Reduction Theorem for Overconvergent $F$-isocrystals over Laurent Series Fields
items.summary: We prove the semistable reduction theorem for $\mathcal{E}^†_K$-valued and $K$-valued overconvergent $F$-isocrystals over $k((t))$-varieties which were introduced by Lazda and Pál. As an application, we prove the finite dimensionality of $\mathcal{E}^†_K$-valued rigid cohomology with compact support.

items.title: Fermat quotients with CM Jacobians and trivial automorphism group
items.summary: Let $F_n$ be the Fermat curve of degree $n$ over $\mathbb Q$, and let $D_n=F_n/S_3$ be its quotient by coordinate permutations. We prove that $D_n$ has trivial geometric automorphism group for every $n\ge 11$ with $\gcd(n,6)=1$. Its Jacobian has complex multiplication. For $n=11$, this Jacobian is absolutely simple of dimension five. We construct an isogeny over $\mathbb Q$ of degree $11^5$ from $\operatorname{Jac}(D_{11})$ to the Jacobian of $y^{11}=x(1-x)^2$. For primes $p\equiv 1\pmod 3$, we also consider the metacyclic quotients $C_p$ of $F_p$ over $\mathbb Q$. By a theorem of Carocca, Lange and Rodríguez, their Jacobians are absolutely simple and have complex multiplication. We prove that $C_p$ has trivial geometric automorphism group if and only if $p\ge 19$. Write $p=r^2+rs+s^2$ with $r,s$ positive integers. The natural degree-three cover $Y_p\to C_p$ satisfies $\operatorname{gon}(Y_p)=r+s$, so $\operatorname{gon}(C_p)\ge \lceil(r+s)/3\rceil$. Since $g(C_p)=(p-1)/6$, both the genus and the gonality of $C_p$ tend to infinity with $p$.

items.title: Finite-coefficient K-theory of henselian valued fields and Gersten injectivity
items.summary: Let $W$ be a henselian valuation ring with fraction field $L$, residue field $k$, and value group $Γ_W$. Let $N=\ell^ν$ be invertible in $W$. Choose an ordered $\mathbf Z/N$-basis $B$ of $Γ_W/NΓ_W$. Products of suitable classes define an equivalence of complete filtered spectra $$ \bigoplus_{\substack{J\subseteq B\\J\text{ finite}}} Σ^{|J|}\operatorname{Fil}_{\mathrm{mot}}^{\bullet-|J|} K(k;\mathbf Z/N) \xrightarrow{\simeq} \operatorname{Fil}_{\mathrm{mot}}^{\bullet} K(L;\mathbf Z/N) $$ The summand indexed by $\varnothing$ is the generic restriction map, after the rigidity equivalence $K(W;\mathbf Z/N)\simeq K(k;\mathbf Z/N)$, and is therefore split injective. Independently of this splitting, excision yields a lifting theorem for regular henselian pairs. In particular, this yields finite-coefficient Gersten injectivity for noetherian henselian regular local rings. Applications to completions along regular primes give relative and sometimes nonhenselian examples. More generally, if $P$ is a Prüfer ring and $R$ is a henselian local ind-smooth $P$-algebra, then $R$ is a domain and $K_n(R;\mathbf Z/N)\to K_n(\operatorname{Frac}(R);\mathbf Z/N)$ is injective for every $n$, provided $N\in R^\times$. These injectivity consequences extend from prime-power to arbitrary finite invertible coefficients by primary decomposition.

items.title: Uniform Three-Fold Product Expansion of Algebraic-Geometry Codes over a Fixed Field
items.summary: A collection of classical codes $C_1,\dots,C_m$ has product expansion if every low-weight word in the sum of their extensions to the product space can be written as a sum of words supported on few lines, each line being a codeword of the corresponding $C_i$. For $m=2$ product expansion is equivalent to robust testability of the tensor code, while for $m\ge 3$ it is strictly stronger; it is the hypothesis on the local codes behind recent constructions of good quantum LDPC codes, good quantum locally testable codes, and quantum codes with transversal non-Clifford gates. No explicit family over a fixed field was previously known to achieve constant rate, linear distance for both the code and its dual, and 3-fold product expansion at growing length. We prove that for the one-point evaluation codes $C_i$ of length $N_i=728\cdot27^{\,i-1}$ and pole order $\lfloor N_i/5\rfloor$ on the Garcia--Stichtenoth tower over $\mathbb{F}_{729}$, the triple $(C_i,C_i,C_i)$ has product expansion with a constant independent of $i$. The dual codes $C_i^\perp$ then form an explicit fixed-field family of rate tending to $109/130$ and relative distance at least $8/65$. The proof is geometric: we view the words of the sum code as arrays on the product of three copies of the $i$-th curve of the tower, where the parity checks are sections of a line bundle. An exact generation theorem describes the sum-code words supported on the grid footprint of a suitable divisor. A support-localisation argument then shows that every low-weight array lies on such a divisor, after deleting a small number of coordinates. We also give a sufficient criterion for three-fold product expansion in terms of degree and genus ratios, yielding explicit families over every non-prime finite field of order at least $512$. The principal conclusions have been formally verified in Lean 4.

items.title: Dense Exact Factorizations of Countable Topological Groups
items.summary: We prove that every countably infinite group endowed with a topology of countable weight in which every nonempty open set is infinite admits an exact factorization into two dense infinite subsets. More generally, every finite partial exact factorization with nonempty factors extends to an exact factorization of the whole group in which both factors meet every member of a prescribed at most countable family of infinite subsets in infinitely many points. This settles the countable case of a question of Protasov and Slobodianiuk. The proof uses the finite graph Ramsey theorem, invariant finitely additive probability measures on amenable groups, and a structural lemma on quadratic coverings based on Neumann's coset covering lemma.

items.title: Nonlinear PDEs with modulated dispersion II: Korteweg-de Vries equation
items.summary: (Due to the limit on the number of characters for an abstract set by arXiv, the full abstract can not be displayed here. See the abstract in the paper.) We study dispersive equations with a time non-homogeneous modulation acting on the linear dispersion term. As primary models, we consider the Korteweg-de Vries equation (KdV) and related equations such as the Benjamin-Ono equation (BO) and the intermediate long wave equation (ILW), imposing certain irregularity conditions on the time non-homogeneous modulation. In this work, we establish phenomena called regularization by noise in three-folds: (i) When the modulation is sufficiently irregular, we show that the modulated KdV on both the circle and the real line is locally well-posed in the regime where the (unmodulated) KdV equation is known to be ill-posed. In particular, given any $s \in \mathbb R$, we show that the modulated KdV on the circle with a sufficiently irregular modulation is locally well-posed in $H^s(\mathbb T)$. Moreover, by adapting the $I$-method to the current modulated setting, we prove global well-posedness of the modulated KdV in negative Sobolev spaces. (ii) It is known that certain (semilinear) dispersive equations such as BO and ILW exhibit quasilinear nature. We show that sufficiently irregular modulations make the modulated versions of these equations semilinear by establishing their local well-posedness by a contraction argument, providing local Lipschitz continuity of the solution map. (iii) We also prove nonlinear smoothing for these modulated equations, where we show that a gain of regularity of the nonlinear part becomes (arbitrarily) larger for more irregular modulations. As applications of our approach, we also include further examples.

items.title: A Second-Order Semi-Implicit Projection Time-Stepping Scheme for the Shallow-Water Equations on the Sphere Using Compatible Finite Elements
items.summary: We propose a second-order, semi-implicit time-stepping scheme for the shallow-water equations on the sphere discretised with compatible finite elements. The scheme splits the advection operator from the wave operator, applying a DG-upwind SSPRK3 method to the advection part and an $H(\text{div})$-conforming implicit discretisation to the wave part, solved efficiently via hybridisation. The scheme follows a three-step symmetric splitting: an explicit half-step, a full advection step, and an implicit half-step that simultaneously projects the velocity back into the $H(\text{div})$ space. This symmetry guarantees global second-order accuracy and confines the stability restriction to the CFL condition of the advection step alone. The time-step can therefore be extended beyond this limit by subcycling the advection step without additional implicit solves. The method is implemented in Firedrake and validated against a standard suite of spherical shallow-water benchmarks, demonstrating stable results for Courant numbers up to 1 (with two advection subcycles) with second-order finite elements, second-order convergence, and good parallel scaling.

items.title: Counting multigeodesics and the Selberg-Delange method
items.summary: We study the counting function $\mathcal{P}^m(X,x)$ for $m$-multigeodesics of length at most $x$ on a compact hyperbolic surface $X$ where $m$ is a positive integer. Building on the Selberg-Delange method, originally developed for counting integers with exactly $m$ prime factors in the interval $[1,x]$, we prove a large $x$ asymptotic for $\mathcal{P}^m(X,x)$. We show that for fixed $m$ as $x\to\infty$ the asymptotic is independent of the surface, whereas for $\frac{m}{\log x}$ bounded away from zero, the asymptotic depends on an infinite Euler product over the lengths of primitive closed geodesics. We also study the distribution of the function $ω_1$, defined on multigeodesics $Γ$ as $ω_1(Γ)=k-1$ for $Γ=(γ_1,...,γ_k)$ a $k$-multigeodesic. We show that as $x\to\infty$, the distribution of $ω_1$ in the set of multigeodesics of length $\leq x$ is close to that of a Poisson random variable with parameter $\log x$. Both of these theorems rely on studying the generating function of the random variable $ω_1$ which we relate to the Selberg zeta function.

items.title: On rigid regular graphs and a problem of Babai and Pultr
items.summary: A graph is rigid if it only admits the identity endomorphism. We show that for every $d\ge 3$ there exist infinitely many mutually rigid $d$-regular graphs of arbitrary odd girth $g\geq 7$. Moreover, we determine the minimum order of a rigid $d$-regular graph for every $d\ge 3$. This provides strong positive answers to a question of van der Zypen [https://mathoverflow.net/q/296483, https://mathoverflow.net/q/321108]. Further, we use our construction to show that every finite monoid is isomorphic to the endomorphism monoid of a regular graph. This solves a problem of Babai and Pultr [J. Comb. Theory, Ser. B, 1980].

items.title: Anabelian perspectives in Galois-Teichmüller theory
items.summary: By exploiting the arithmetic homotopy of the moduli spaces of curves, Galois-Teichmüller theory stands at the interface of braid-mapping class groups and of anabelian geometry. Starting from the classical braid-theoretic construction of the Grothendieck-Teichmüller group, we review how anabelian geometry -- beginning with the foundational work of Nakamura -- provides the arithmetic mechanisms underlying its definition. We then explain how the combinatorial anabelian geometry developed by Hoshi and Mochizuki recasts these constructions within a purely group-theoretic and algorithmic framework. In particular, we describe how the group GT emerges as an anabelian object and how, once freed from an auxiliary or artificially imposed containers, the anabelian algorithms yield a combinatorial reconstruction of the absolute Galois group of rational numbers. The perspective developed here highlights a conceptual shift from explicit braid-theoretic computations to functorial and algorithmic forms of anabelian reconstruction.

items.title: Perfect Codes As Exact Minimizers Of Quadratic Discrepancy In q-ary Hamming Spaces
items.summary: Total quadratic ball discrepancy measures the deviation of codeword counts from uniformity over all Hamming balls. We prove that, whenever a Hamming space and cardinality admit a perfect code, the discrepancy minimizers among all subsets of that cardinality are precisely the perfect codes. This extends Barg's binary minimizing result and characterizes equality over arbitrary finite alphabets. At parameter sets that satisfy the sphere-packing condition and Lloyd's integral-root condition for correcting one or two errors, we give an explicit lower bound whose attainment is equivalent to perfect tiling: the discrepancy that a perfect code with these parameters would have. For one error, these include parameters at which the existence of a perfect code is open. For alphabets of size at least four, the discrepancy is an affine function of an energy with a strictly completely monotonic potential; for these alphabets, known universal energy bounds also give these lower bounds, and, when a perfect code exists, known universal optimality results also give the characterization of the minimizers. Over the ternary alphabet, complete monotonicity fails, and we prove the ternary bounds directly at all Hamming parameters and at the Golay parameters, the only nontrivial ternary cases.

items.title: A note on general isolation result in Diophantine Approximation
items.summary: In the present paper we give very simple general statements which deal with approximation of a real number by rationals and are related to isolation phenomenon. In particular we study functions $ f(x)>f_1(x)>0$ such that existence of solutions $\frac{p}{q}$ of Diophantine inequality $ \left| α-\frac{p}{q}\right|< \frac{f(q)}{q^2} $ leads to the existence of solutions of inequality $ \left| α-\frac{p}{q}\right|< \frac{f_1(q)}{q^2} $.

items.title: Spectral Thresholds in Correlated Spiked Models and Fundamental Limits of Partial Least Squares
items.summary: We provide a rigorous random matrix theory analysis of spiked cross-covariance models where the signals across two high-dimensional data channels are partially aligned. These models are motivated by multi-modal learning and form the standard generative setting underlying Partial Least Squares (PLS), a widely used yet theoretically underdeveloped method. We show that the leading singular values of the sample cross-covariance matrix undergo a Baik-Ben Arous-Peche (BBP)-type phase transition, and we characterize the precise thresholds for the emergence of informative components. Our results yield the first sharp asymptotic description of the signal recovery capabilities of PLS in this setting, revealing a fundamental performance gap between PLS and the Bayes-optimal estimator. In particular, we identify the SNR and correlation regimes where PLS fails to recover any signal, despite detectability being possible in principle. These findings clarify the theoretical limits of PLS and provide guidance for the design of reliable multi-modal inference methods in high dimensions.

items.title: Non-Isothermal Plane Couette Flow for the Boltzmann Equation in Three Dimensions
items.summary: We study the Boltzmann equation for a non-isothermal plane Couette flow in the three-dimensional channel $\mathbb T_x\times(-1,1)_y\times\mathbb T_z$ for Maxwell molecules. For sufficiently small shear rate and wall temperature perturbations, we construct a unique steady solution near the global Maxwellian. For the corresponding unsteady boundary value problem, we establish the global existence and uniqueness of solutions arising from small perturbations of the steady state, together with their exponential convergence to the steady state as $t\to\infty$. A major difficulty in both the steady and unsteady problems is to close the outgoing mass fluxes generated by diffuse reflection. To overcome this difficulty, we develop a new boundary flux transmission framework which, in the slab geometry, yields steady and time-dependent wall flux estimates through the boundary-to-boundary transmission between the two walls. We further extend this framework to damped transport equations with diffuse reflection in general bounded $C^1$ domains, even when the damping coefficient degenerates at large velocities.

items.title: Minimal Filling Architectures for Polynomial Neural Networks
items.summary: Minimal filling architectures describe the smallest hidden-layer widths for which the neurovariety of a polynomial neural network fills its ambient function space. It was conjectured that every such architecture has unimodal hidden widths. We construct counterexamples to this conjecture using a frontier search and certify the main example through finite-field Jacobian computations and recursive dimension bounds. In the opposite direction, we prove that every minimal filling architecture of depth at most three is unimodal. A nonunimodal minimal filling architecture of depth four shows that the depth bound is sharp.

items.title: Hyper Input Convex Neural Networks for Shape Constrained Learning and Optimal Transport
items.summary: We introduce Hyper Input Convex Neural Networks (HyCNNs), a novel neural network architecture designed for learning convex functions. HyCNNs combine the principles of Maxout networks with input convex neural networks (ICNNs) to create a neural network that is always convex in the input, theoretically capable of leveraging depth, and performs reliably when trained at scale compared to ICNNs. Concretely, we prove that HyCNNs require exponentially fewer parameters than ICNNs to approximate quadratic functions up to a given precision. Throughout a series of synthetic experiments, we demonstrate that HyCNNs outperform existing ICNNs and MLPs in terms of predictive performance for convex regression and interpolation tasks. We further apply HyCNNs to learn high-dimensional optimal transport maps for synthetic examples and for single-cell data, where they oftentimes outperform ICNN-based neural optimal transport methods and other baselines across a wide range of setting.

items.title: Mirror Descent-Ascent for mean-field min-max problems
items.summary: We study two variants of the mirror descent-ascent (MDA) algorithm for solving min-max problems on the space of measures: simultaneous and alternating. We work under assumptions of convexity-concavity and relative smoothness of the payoff function with respect to a suitable Bregman divergence, defined on the space of measures via flat derivatives. We establish non-asymptotic convergence rates to mixed Nash equilibria, measured in the Nikaidô-Isoda error, proving an $\mathcal{O}(N^{-1/2})$ rate for simultaneous MDA and an improved $\mathcal{O}(N^{-2/3})$ rate for alternating MDA. The main technical contribution is an infinite-dimensional dual space analysis that relates Bregman divergences on measures to dual Bregman divergences on spaces of bounded continuous functions, allowing us to control asymmetric commutator terms created by alternating updates. The results substantially generalize prior analyses restricted to bilinear objectives and also apply to nonlinear convex-concave problems on measure spaces, thereby providing a unified theoretical foundation for MDA in mean-field min-max optimization.

items.title: A simplified proof of the o-minimal Whitney Extension Theorem
items.summary: We give a proof of the o-minimal version of the Whitney Extension Theorem simplified as compared to the original ones. A new simplifying ingredient is a definable variant of Urysohn's lemma for class $\mathcal{C}^q$ (see Section 3).

items.title: Classification of analytic $\text{SO}^o(p,q)$-actions on closed $(p+q-1)$-dimensional manifolds II : $p \geq 3$, $q=1,2$
items.summary: This paper provides a classification of analytic actions of the semi-orthogonal groups $\text{SO}^\circ(p,1)$ and $\text{SO}^\circ(p,2)$, for $p \geq 3$, on closed, connected manifolds of dimension $p$ and $p+1$ respectively. It is a sequel to a previous paper, which treats the case $p,q \geq 3$. Adapting Uchida's methods, we explicitly construct analytic actions of $\text{SO}^\circ(p,1)$ on $\text{S}^{p}$ and $\text{S}^{p-1} \times \text{S}^{1}$, and analytic actions of $\text{SO}^\circ(p,2)$ on $\text{S}^{p+1}$, $\text{S}^{p} \times \text{S}^{1}$ and $\text{S}^{p-1} \times \text{S}^{2}$, and we classify them up to analytic isomorphism, using a result of Hitchin and Schneider's classification of analytic $\text{SL}_2(\mathbb{R})$ actions on surfaces. The main result demonstrates that any analytic $\text{SO}^\circ(p,q)$ action, $q=1,2$, on a closed, connected $(p+q-1)$-dimensional manifold is covered by one of the constructed actions or by an action on $\text{SO}^\circ(p,q) \times_P \text{S}^1$, where $P$ is a maximal parabolic subgroup of $\text{SO}^\circ(p,q)$.

items.title: Exponential Consensus and Flocking in Multi-Agent Systems with Infinite Fading Memory
items.summary: In this paper, we study the emergent collective dynamics of multi-agent systems driven by infinite distributed fading memory of Volterra type. We establish a unified theoretical framework covering both first-order opinion consensus dynamics and second-order velocity alignment flocking kinematics. By introducing Dafermos past-history transformations, the governing integro-differential systems are reformulated into dynamical systems on extended product Hilbert spaces. For first-order dynamics, we prove that fading memory inherently provides a hidden dissipative mechanism, guaranteeing unconditional global exponential consensus with or without instantaneous communication forces. For second-order dynamics, by developing a unified energy-multiplier framework that seamlessly couples instantaneous communication with memory dissipation, we establish unconditional global exponential flocking for both the pure fading memory system and the mixed interaction system, completely independent of the spatial dispersion or the communication tail.

items.title: Worst-Case Finite-Horizon Analysis of Perturbed LQR via Performance Estimation Problem
items.summary: We propose a framework to assess the robustness of a given state-feedback controller by evaluating its worst-case finite-horizon cost over a class of norm-bounded perturbations. To compute this cost, we show how to apply the Performance Estimation Problem (PEP) framework, originally developed to analyze optimization algorithms, and reformulate the worst-case search as a rank-constrained Semidefinite Program (SDP). Our results suggest that the perturbations that induce the highest finite-horizon costs can differ substantially from those identified using standard asymptotic metrics. Intuitively, worst-case perturbations are obtained by aligning slowly decaying modes with specific initial conditions to drive transient growth, causing a bifurcation in the worst-case behavior as the horizon length changes. These findings open new possibilities to certify finite-horizon performance of broader system classes, including data-driven models or nonlinear components.

items.title: Uniqueness and nondegeneracy for a critical Choquard equation with Hardy potential
items.summary: We study the critical Choquard equation \[ -Δu-μ|x|^{-2}u =\bigl(|\cdot|^{2-N}*|u|^p\bigr)|u|^{p-2}u \qquad\text{in }\mathbb R^N, \] where $|\cdot|^{2-N}$ is the Newton kernel, $p=\frac{N+2}{N-2}$, and $0<μ<\frac{(N-2)^2}{4}$. For every $N\ge3$, we prove that positive solutions in $D^{1,2}(\mathbb R^N)$ are radially symmetric about the origin, unique up to dilation, and nondegenerate. Our proof uses normalized logarithmic derivatives to obtain a cooperative system. The resulting monotonicity principle underlies both the uniqueness and nondegeneracy arguments, and remains effective in the subquadratic range $1<p<2$, corresponding to $N\ge7$. Consequently, the linearized quadratic form has Morse index one and the sharp inequality admits a global quadratic remainder estimate. The best constant is strictly concave in the Hardy parameter on $\bigl[0,\frac{(N-2)^2}{4}\bigr)$, is of class $C^2$ with strictly negative second derivative in the interior, and satisfies two-sided bounds that agree to first order at $μ=0$.

items.title: First-Order Model Checking on Monadically Dependent Graph Classes
items.summary: Monadically dependent graph classes are those in which first-order logic cannot encode all graphs. They include all nowhere dense classes and all classes of bounded twin-width. We show that first-order model checking is fixed-parameter tractable on every monadically dependent graph class. Together with the known hardness result for hereditary classes that are not monadically dependent, this gives a complete characterization of the hereditary graph classes with fixed-parameter tractable first-order model checking. This resolves a central open problem in algorithmic model theory. Our proof combines ideas from structural graph theory (graph decompositions), finite model theory (locality of first-order logic), and model theory (counting types). In particular, we show that in monadically dependent classes, tuples of fixed length have only $|U|^{O(1)}$ types of fixed quantifier rank over any set of parameters $U$.

items.title: The kinetic Kato square root problem
items.summary: We solve the kinetic Kato square root problem for the whole-space Kolmogorov operator $$H_A=\partial_t-X\cdot\nabla_Y-\operatorname{div}_X(A\nabla_X)$$ on \(\mathrm L^2\) with Lebesgue measure, where \(A\) is a bounded measurable complex uniformly accretive matrix depending on all variables. We define its realization through a sesquilinear form and identify the square-root domains of the resulting maximal accretive operator and its adjoint with the intrinsic Sobolev space defined by one velocity derivative and half a derivative along the transport flow. The homogeneous norm equivalences depend only on the dimension and the coefficient bounds. The energy also controls a position derivative of order one third. The proof uses second-order resolvents and localized affine testing. A regularized transport symmetrizer gives hidden coercivity, while comparison with a positive Rockland operator supplies intrinsic smoothing. Commutator and dyadic approximation estimates remove the smoothing before a Carleson argument is applied. We also obtain uniform shifted square-root estimates and bounded velocity, transport and position Riesz transforms.

items.title: Hodge--Riemann relations for $m$-positive and generalized $m$-positive forms
items.summary: We study Hodge--Riemann relations for ordinary, sequential, and weak $m$-positive real $(1,1)$-forms in complex dimension $d$. For ordinary $m$-positive forms, we prove the fully mixed relations in every permitted bidegree without assuming semipositivity, generalizing results by Xiao. As a generalization of ordinary $m$-positivity, sequential $m$-positivity is defined by the hyperbolicity cones of successive directional derivatives of the determinant. We formulate a generalized mixed Hodge--Riemann conjecture for this condition and prove several cases beyond the scalar inequalities supplied by hyperbolicity. We prove strict strong positivity for good prefixes with at most three repeated blocks after the first factor. We also consider weak $m$-positivity which corresponds to the pointwise subsolution condition for the complex $m$-Hessian equation. In this setting, we prove the Hodge--Riemann relations for $p\neq q$ and in several diagonal cases, and show that the associated power map induces a pointwise diffeomorphism onto the cone of positive $(d-1,d-1)$-forms. Using Dinh and Nguyên's $L^2$ globalization method, we pass from the pointwise relations to cohomology classes on compact Kähler manifolds. Finally, we propose conjectures on a numerical criterion for sequential $m$-positive classes and on the solvability of the generalized $m$-Hessian equation.

items.title: Necessary and sufficient conditions for the self-normalized central limit theorem for independent triangular arrays
items.summary: For a rowwise independent triangular array $\{X_{n,i}:1\le i\le n\}$, put $S_n=\sum_{i=1}^nX_{n,i}$ and $V_n^2=\sum_{i=1}^nX_{n,i}^2$. We prove that $S_n/V_n\xrightarrow{\mathrm d}{\mathrm N}(0,1)$ implies $\max_{i\le n}|X_{n,i}|/V_n\xrightarrow{\mathbb P}0$. The same assumption gives $V_n^2/b_n^2\xrightarrow{\mathbb P}1$ for any choice of medians $b_n^2$ of $V_n^2$. Combined with the results of Shao (2018), this yields necessary and sufficient conditions for the self-normalized central limit theorem and resolves his conjecture for independent sequences. The proof identifies the joint limits of the sum and its sum of squares, then uses the standard normal ratio to remove every non-Gaussian component.

items.title: Linear bounds and sharp exponential growth for commuting matrix algebra
items.summary: For any $m$ pairwise commuting matrices $\{A_i\}_{i=1}^{m}\subset \M_n(\F)$, we prove $\dim_\F \F[A_1,\cdots, A_m]\leq (2^m-1)(n-1)+1$, answering Bergman's question on the existence of a linear bound for a fixed number $m$.

items.title: The first gap for minimal submanifolds in spheres
items.summary: Let $f:M^n\to\Sn^{n+q}(1)$ be a minimal immersion of a closed connected manifold with $n\ge3$ and $q\ge2$, and let $S$ be the squared length of its second fundamental form. We prove an integral inequality that gives $\max_M S\ge n$ if the immersion is not totally geodesic. If $n\ne4$ or $q=2$, equality $\max_M S=n$ holds if and only if the immersion is a Clifford minimal hypersurface; if $n=4$ and $q\ge3$, equality holds if and only if the immersion is a Clifford minimal hypersurface or the standard minimal embedding of $\mathbb{CP}^2$ in $\Sn^7(1)$. Both classifications are understood up to an ambient isometry, a totally geodesic inclusion, and a finite covering. We construct the integral inequalities using polynomial weights and divergence identities. The required algebraic estimates are proved by sums of squared tensor norms.

items.title: Categorified convergence: dropping the 'ultra' from 'virtual ultracategories'
items.summary: Virtual ultracategories are a recent categorification of topological spaces seen as sets of points together with a convergence relation between points and ultrafilters. However, a topology can also be described in terms of convergence of filters: in this paper, we thus introduce an analogue of virtual ultracategories based on filters rather than ultrafilters. At the topological level, convergence of filters is completely determined by its restriction to ultrafilters. Our main result shows that, under the assumption of tautness, the same phenomenon holds at the categorified level, thereby offering a non-ultra-biased perspective on virtual ultracategories.

items.title: Adaptive pairwise preference elicitation for decision support: identifying the best alternative with fewer judgments
items.summary: Interactive decision support systems often require repeated preference judgments, although identifying the best alternative may not justify eliciting all \(n(n-1)/2\) pairwise comparisons. We propose ALEC (Adaptive Lexicographic Elicitation of Comparisons), which re-ranks the alternatives after each judgment and asks the first unobserved pair in the lexicographic order of the current ranking, using the Analytic Hierarchy Process as the concrete setting. Under a log-normal error model, directly comparing a contrast maximises the one-step reduction in its effective resistance. Posterior bounds on the probability of a wrong choice or of exceeding a relative-loss tolerance provide stopping rules valid under adaptive questioning, while a consistency-and-margin condition gives a deterministic certificate of agreement with the full-matrix winner. Simulations show that re-ranking is most useful in larger problems with limited budgets; ALEC outperforms Harker's original rule in most scenarios with \(n\ge11\), while under a common stopping rule it achieves higher hit-rate point estimates than the stronger Harker-log variant at a modest additional questioning cost. With a 5\% loss tolerance and a cap of \(2n\) additional comparisons, the stopping rule saves \res{prot-s06-saveadd-min}--\res{prot-s06-saveadd-max}\% of them, while among runs stopped by the bound the observed rate of losses above tolerance remains at most \res{s06-errearly-max}\%, against a nominal 10\%. ALEC therefore provides an adaptive elicitation module for decision support systems that balances decision precision against user effort.

items.title: Convergence and Stability of a Catching-Up Algorithm for Differential Inclusions with Maximally Monotone Operators
items.summary: We study a catching-up algorithm with approximate projections for finite-dimensional differential inclusions governed by a maximally monotone operator and a continuous perturbation. Through the canonical decomposition of the operator into a regular part and the normal cone to the closure of its domain, the problem becomes a sweeping process, discretized by an explicit predictor step and a feasible approximate projection. For variable time steps, the approximations converge, up to a subsequence, to a solution on every finite horizon when the mesh size and the accumulated projection-error budget vanish and the nodes stay in a common compact convex set. This set comes from linear growth on finite horizons and, without any growth condition, by dissipativity of the projected field at a feasible center, which confines the nodes to a fixed ball uniformly in time for small steps and small projection errors. Under either condition, locally Lipschitz perturbations give global well-posedness, convergence of the whole family, and, for a common initial state, a trajectory-error estimate of order $O(\sqrt{h+E})$, where $h$ is the maximal step and $E$ the accumulated budget; sparse projection errors are allowed. An elastic network with unilateral stops illustrates the results, and numerical experiments compare the algorithm with the full-resolvent discretization.

items.title: Overcoming Fundamental Control Limitations in Powered Descent Flight through Robust Incremental Nonlinear Dynamic Inversion
items.summary: This work identifies a fundamental, controller-independent limitation in reusable launch vehicle powered descent: a sudden $180^\circ$ phase transition in the open-loop transfer functions from the control inputs to the lateral drift and drift rate. The transition occurs inside the flight envelope, reverses the effective control direction, and can destabilize the closed loop system under uncertainty. An analytical condition governing this transition is derived, its physical mechanism is established, and its dependence on vehicle mass, aerodynamic properties, and geometry is characterized. An Incremental Nonlinear Dynamic Inversion (INDI)-based control architecture is then developed to inherently address this limitation and is tuned via $\mathcal{H}_\infty$ Closed Loop Shaping to provide local robustness and performance guarantees. The internal dynamics introduced by the INDI inversion are analytically derived and proven to be stable throughout the flight envelope. The proposed controller is compared against a robust gain-scheduled baseline controller through linear stability analysis and an extensive nonlinear Monte Carlo campaign. Both controllers achieve 100% success across the considered Monte Carlo campaign, though the INDI-based controller provides improved tracking performance, superior nominal and dispersed stability margins, requires fewer controller design points, and reduces controller tuning complexity.

items.title: Classifying Leibniz racks
items.summary: Lie quandles were defined by T. Fritz as a nonlinear generalization of Lie algebras, to serve as a nonlinear algebras of observables in generalized form of Hamiltonian mechanics. These objects were subsequently generalized in a prequel article to objects referred to as smooth Lie group families of smooth racks by the authors. In this article, we investigate a particular system of nonlinear functional differential equations whose solution in general provides a pathway to the classification of smooth Lie group families of smooth rack structures on any given smooth manifold. We then discuss a particularly practical ansatz for solving these equations, and use it to construct new families of examples, as well as prove a result on the sense in which the Bloch sphere is the unique Lie quandle structure on the sphere.

items.title: The infinitude of square-free palindromes
items.summary: We settle an open problem regarding palindromes; that is, positive integers which are the same when written forwards and backwards. In particular, we prove that for any fixed base $b\geq 2$, there exist infinitely many square-free palindromes in base $b$. We also provide an asymptotic expression for the number of such integers $\leq x$. The core of our proof utilises a hybrid $p$-adic/Archimedean van der Corput process, used in conjunction with an equidistribution estimate of Tuxanidy and Panario, as well as an elementary argument of Cilleruelo, Luca and Shparlinski.

items.title: Characterization of Fréchet Spaces and Application to Hausdorff MNC
items.summary: We study the Hausdorff measure of noncompactness associated with compatible metrics on Fréchet spaces, with the aim of extending its Banach-space properties. After recalling the characterization by complete translation-invariant metrics with convex balls, we calculate the scalar Hausdorff measure for a standard weighted fractional metric. For bounded nonprecompact sets its value is the unique root of an equation involving a finite seminorm gauge determined by the covering radius. This yields an actual Hausdorff-condensing criterion for compact perturbations of maps having separate contraction constants at the seminorm levels. On countable products of Banach spaces we obtain an exact coordinate formula and a sharp scalar contraction bound on bounded domains, without requiring a uniform gap between the coordinate constants and one for strict condensation. For closed subspaces, an exact finite-projection formula retains the compatibility constraints on covering centers. Explicit examples show why separately computed seminorm measures cannot generally be substituted into the metric formula. Applications to spaces of real sequence-valued continuous functions give an explicit oscillation formula and exhibit the compatibility obstruction on an unbounded interval. Classical fixed-point consequences are recorded briefly.

items.title: A two-stage approach to satellite constellation optimization: classical and QUBO formulations
items.summary: The design of satellite constellations for Earth observation requires balancing spatial coverage, revisit time, cost, and operational complexity. This paper considers the problem of designing the orbits of a given number of Low Earth Orbit (LEO) or Very Low Earth Orbit (VLEO) satellites to maximize the spatial and temporal resolution achieved over a prescribed set of ground targets. This kind of problem is inherently nonconvex and possibly combinatorial, making its solution computationally demanding for large constellations and target sets. To address this challenge, we propose a two-stage optimization strategy that separates spatial-coverage design from temporal-resolution optimization, thereby reducing the complexity of the overall problem. Two variants of the method are developed. The first employs continuous decision variables during the spatial-optimization stage, whereas the second discretizes these variables and reformulates the problem as a Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) problem. The latter formulation enables the use of efficient classical QUBO solvers and is directly compatible with quantum-annealing hardware. The proposed framework provides a scalable approach to the design of heterogeneous LEO and VLEO Earth-observation constellations and establishes a pathway for exploiting emerging quantum-optimization technologies in satellite mission design. Preliminary simulation results are presented to demonstrate the effectiveness of the strategy.

items.title: Proof of the Harary--Hill conjecture: an exposition
items.summary: The Harary--Hill conjecture states that the crossing number of the complete graph $K_n$ is exactly $\frac{1}{4}\left\lfloor\frac{n}{2}\right\rfloor \left\lfloor\frac{n-1}{2}\right\rfloor \left\lfloor\frac{n-2}{2}\right\rfloor \left\lfloor\frac{n-3}{2}\right\rfloor$. We present a streamlined variant of the proof of this conjecture recently announced by OpenAI (2026). Although the original proof is relatively short, it is quite difficult to follow. We simplify several steps and provide a concise and accessible exposition of the proof. We also combine this new result with known reductions to determine the crossing numbers of several other graph families.

items.title: The Calkin--Wilf problems on $\ell$-ary partition functions
items.summary: In their 1998 precursor to their celebrated paper ``Recounting the rationals,'' Calkin and Wilf listed nine open problems related to the function $b_{k,\ell}(n)$, the number of partitions of $n$ into powers of $\ell$ with each part appearing at most $k$ times. In this short paper, we answer five of their eight remaining open problems. As a consequence of our results, we extend and generalise results of both Carlitz and Reznick, and answer an open question of Reznick.

items.title: Stable and Gaussian Fluctuation Limit of a Lévy-Driven Slow-Fast System
items.summary: We study fluctuation limit of a slow-fast system driven by $α$-stable Lévy noise with $1<α<2.$ The slow component is generated by an odd polynomial function $f(y):=y^q,$ while in the fast component, the drift is $g(y):=-|y|^p\operatorname{sgn}(y)$ for some $p>0.$ Although the noise is given, the fluctuation limit is either a stable process or a Brownian motion, depending on both $p$ and $α.$ The critical line between stable limit and Brownian limit is $q+1-p=α/2.$

items.title: Non-simple blow-up for the Chern--Simons--Higgs equation on Riemannian surfaces
items.summary: The existence and structure of non-simple blow-up are fundamental questions for the self-dual Chern--Simons--Higgs equation. Physically, this phenomenon describes magnetic-flux concentration in several cores whose mutual distances are much larger than their widths, although all cores approach the same vortex point. Despite substantial progress for singular Liouville equations, the existence of non-simple blow-up solutions to the full Chern--Simons--Higgs equation on closed surfaces has remained open in both the Chern--Simons (CS) and mean-field regimes. We prove that the cores of every non-simple cluster have equal limiting masses, share a common profile type, and form an asymptotically regular polygon. These identities yield an explicit finite list of admissible cluster masses and a four-unit mass-gap criterion. We also construct non-simple blow-up solutions on closed Riemannian surfaces in both regimes. Together, these results establish a sharp arithmetic criterion for single-point non-simple CS blow-up on each fixed flat torus when a suitable exterior divisor may be chosen, and show that vortex blow-up need not be simple, answering Li--Liu's question in the negative.

items.title: The Short Pulse equation on the half lines: a Riemann--Hilbert approach
items.summary: In this work, we analyze the initial boundary value (IBV) problems for the Short Pulse (SP) equation $u_{xt}=u+\frac{1}{6}(u^3)_{xx}$ (classical solutions) on the half-lines $x\ge 0$ and $x\le 0$ under the condition of sufficient decay as $x\to +\infty$ or as $x\to -\infty$. Using the Riemann--Hilbert (RH) problem approach, we show that these two IBV problems differ substantially regarding the boundary values required for problems to be well-posed. Namely, the solution of the ``right problem'' ($x\ge 0$) is uniquely determined by the initial data $u(x,0)$, $x\ge 0$ alone, whereas for the ``left problem'' ($x\le 0$), two boundary functions $u(0,t)$ and $u_x(0,t)$ have to be prescribed, together with the initial data, for a well-posed problem.

items.title: On the Minimal Controllability of Boolean Networks With $k$-Regular Dependency Graphs
items.summary: Boolean networks (BNs) are widely used to model gene regulatory networks and other biological systems. In this paper, we investigate the minimal controllability problem for BNs subject to degree constraints. We first establish three new best-case upper bounds for XOR-BNs whose dependency graphs are $k$-regular. We then introduce classes of BNs that are invariant under cyclically partite transformation (CPT-invariant) and prove theorems connecting BN controllability with the surjectivity of vector-valued Boolean functions. Finally, by combining an analysis of this surjectivity with a probabilistic argument, we derive a new general lower bound on the minimum number of control nodes required for majority-type threshold BNs with $(2k+1)$-regular dependency graphs.

items.title: PCF All The Way Down
items.summary: We prove that a finite surjective post-critically finite self-map of a variety in characteristic zero remains post-critically finite on every preperiodic integral effective divisor after passing to its periodic image with its return map. Iterating this result proves PCF all the way down. A detailed report on AI usage is contained in the manuscript.

items.title: Isosceles sets and two-distance sets in Euclidean space
items.summary: A finite set of points in $\mathbb{R}^d$ is isosceles if every three of its points form an isosceles triangle. Erdős asked in 1946 for the largest size $\mathrm{iso}(d)$ of an isosceles set in $\mathbb{R}^d$; the answer was known for $d\le8$. Let $g(d)$ and $M(d)$ be the largest sizes of a two-distance set and of a spherical two-distance set in $\mathbb{R}^d$. We prove that $\mathrm{iso}(d)=\max\{g(d),M(d)+1,M(d-1)+3\}$ for every $d\ge2$, which reduces the problem to these two classical ones. With the recently determined values of $g(d)$ for $9\le d\le22$ we obtain $\mathrm{iso}(d)=\binom{d+1}{2}+1$ for $9\le d\le21$ and $\mathrm{iso}(22)=276$, and we show that the extremal set is unique: for $d\le21$ it is the set of midpoints of the edges of a regular simplex together with its centroid, and for $d=22$ it is the McLaughlin configuration together with its centre. For $10\le d\le22$ every isosceles set with more than $\binom d2+3$ points is a two-distance set or a spherical two-distance set together with its centre. The proofs start from Blokhuis' decomposition of isosceles sets into mutually orthogonal two-distance sets. Counting leaves one configuration open: a two-distance set with $\binom{d+1}{2}$ points in a hyperplane, the largest number allowed by Blokhuis' bound, together with two points that are mirror images of each other. We exclude it by showing that a two-distance set $T$ attaining Blokhuis' bound in $\mathbb{R}^n$ is unisolvent for quadratic polynomials and that, if $T$ lies on two concentric spheres, then apart from two exceptional cases its two layers are spherical $2$-designs whose sizes are determined by the radii. We also show that the squared distances of such a set are in ratio $(k-1):k$ with $(2k-1)^2\le n+1$ if $n\ge9$. Hence there is none for $9\le n\le23$, so that $g(23)\le299$ and $\mathrm{iso}(23)=\max\{g(23),278\}\le299$.

items.title: Tree embeddings and nonuniqueness in site percolation
items.summary: Let $G$ be an infinite connected simple graph of minimum degree at least seven. Suppose $G$ is embedded in the plane so that every compact set meets only finitely many vertices and edges. We prove that $p_c^{\mathrm{site}}(G)<1/2$ and that, for every $p_c^{\mathrm{site}}(G)<p<1-p_c^{\mathrm{site}}(G)$, Bernoulli$(p)$ site percolation almost surely has infinitely many infinite open clusters. We also construct a subtree of $G$ with critical site percolation probability $\sqrt{2}-1$. We prove a general stability theorem for infinite connected locally finite graphs $G\subseteq H$ on the same vertex set. Suppose that, at parameter $a\in(0,1)$, the probability that a deterministic finite set meets an infinite open cluster in $G$ tends uniformly to one as its size grows. Then, for each fixed $b\in(a,1]$, under the standard monotone coupling, almost surely every infinite open cluster in $H$ at parameter $b$ contains an infinite open cluster in $G$ at parameter $a$. No planarity, transitivity, or uniform degree bound is required. Finally, we obtain a lower bound on two-point connectivity under uniqueness for arbitrary infinite locally finite graphs, yielding a general criterion for nonuniqueness.

items.title: Semigroups of matrices with dense orbits (revised version)
items.summary: For $\mathbb{K}=\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and every $n\ge 1$ we construct two $n\times n$ matrices $A$ and $B$ such that the orbit of every vector $p\in\mathbb{K}^n$ with $p_1\ne 0$ under the semigroup generated by $A$ and $B$ is dense in $\mathbb{K}^n$; the remaining vectors lie in an invariant hyperplane, so the set of vectors with dense orbit is exactly the complement of a hyperplane. Thus two generators always suffice for a hypercyclic semigroup of matrices, in contrast with the commutative case, where $n+1$ generators are needed on $\mathbb{C}^n$. We give a transparent reformulation of the hypotheses, a criterion for the density of $\{a^mb^n\}$ that makes them checkable, and explicit examples with complete proofs. As applications we obtain affine pairs on $\mathbb{K}^n$ all of whose orbits are dense, and, for every $n$, a pair of real matrices with an orbit that is somewhere dense but not dense in $\mathbb{R}^n$.

items.title: Higher-Order Neyman Orthogonality in Moment-Condition Models
items.summary: We construct moment functions that are Neyman-orthogonal to a chosen order in moment-condition models that involve finite-dimensional nuisance parameters. These moment functions reduce sensitivity to estimation error in the nuisance parameters and, as such, offer a unified and tractable route to higher-order debiasing in a wide range of econometric models. The number of additional nuisance parameters required by our construction, beyond those already present in the original moment conditions, is independent of the order of orthogonalization and can be reduced to a single scalar if desired.

items.title: A Solution Method for Single-Source Capacitated Facility Location Problems Under Decision-Dependent Demand Uncertainty
items.summary: We present a model and an exact solution method for single-source capacitated facility location problems with decision-dependent demand uncertainty. The model allows the joint probability distribution of customer demands to depend on the facility to which demand points are allocated. The number of possible decision-dependent distributions is therefore equal to the number of feasible allocations of demand points to (groups of) facilities. To address the exponential size of the model, we apply and extend a recent version of the L-Shaped method for stochastic programs with decision-dependent uncertainty. In particular,we compare the original optimality cut with a new optimality cut based on a bilinear reformulation. We prove that, separated together with the original one, the new cut yields a tighter restriction, at the expense of introducing bilinear terms. In addition, we prove an effective decision-independent valid inequality that significantly improves convergence. Extensive numerical tests on 180 instances demonstrate that the method, supported by the valid inequality, can find optimal or near-optimal solutions to problem instances with up to 620 potential probability distributions. The tests also show that, while the new cut closes slightly more instances, the original cut remains preferable in terms of solution time and optimality gap.

items.title: Flexible $3$-valent graphs of arbitrary girth
items.summary: We prove the existence of a finite connected flexible $3$-valent vertex-transitive graph of girth $\ell$ for every integer $\ell \geq 3$.

items.title: Idiosynchromatic Poetry
items.summary: We prove equivalences of asymmetric partition relations involving natural numbers and products of weakly compact cardinals $κ$, infinite cardinals $λ<κ$ and natural numbers to certain classes of finitary problems in the theory of edge-coloured digraphs. We are able to determine three classes of Ramsey numbers exactly, typical examples in these classes are $r(ω^2 2, 3)$, $r(κλ2, 3)$ and $r(κλ3, 3)$. We moreover provide general upper bounds for $r(ω^2 m, 3)$ and $r(κλm, n)$.

items.title: Quadratic-size Random Permutations are Universal
items.summary: A permutation is $n$-universal if it contains every permutation of length $n$ as a pattern. We prove that a uniformly random permutation of length $32n^2$ is $n$-universal with probability at least $1-\exp(-n/25)$ for all sufficiently large $n$. This removes a $\log\log n$ factor from an earlier result of He and Kwan~\cite{He-Kwan} and resolves an open problem of Alon~\cite{Alon2016}. The proof was found by GPT-6 Pro.

items.title: Relative Tate-Shafarevich kernel of a reductive group over a global field
items.summary: We describe an algorithm and a computer program computing the relative Tate-Shafarevich kernel $Sha^S(K,G)$ of a reductive group $G$ over a global field $K$ with respect to a finite set $S$ of places of $K$ containing no archimedean places. We assume that we know the algebraic fundamental group $Λ=π_1^{alg}(G)$ together with the action on it of the Galois group $Θ=Gal(L/K)$, where $L/K$ is a finite Galois extension with no real places such that $Gal(K^s/L)$ acts trivially on $Λ$. We also assume that we know the decomposition subgroups $Θ_v\subseteq Θ$ for all places $v$ in $S$, and all non-cyclic decomposition subgroups $Θ_v$ for $v$ outside $S$. Under certain conditions, we compute the set $Sha^S(K,G)$ also when $S$ contains archimedean places.

items.title: Sharp moderate deviations and uniform Berry--Esseen bounds for Hotelling's $T^2$-statistic via Stein's method
items.summary: Let $\mathbf X_1,\ldots,\mathbf X_n$ be independent random vectors in $\mathbb R^d$ with common mean $\boldsymbolμ_n$, where $d\ge2$ is a fixed integer. Let $\bar{\mathbf X}_n=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf X_i$ denote the sample mean and let \[ \widehatΣ_n=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n (\mathbf X_i-\bar{\mathbf X}_n) (\mathbf X_i-\bar{\mathbf X}_n)^\top \] denote the sample covariance matrix. Assume that the average covariance matrix is positive definite and that $\widehatΣ_n$ is nonsingular almost surely. For testing $H_0:\boldsymbolμ_n=\boldsymbolμ_0$, the Hotelling statistic is \[ T^2_{H,n} =n(\bar{\mathbf X}_n-\boldsymbolμ_0)^\top \widehatΣ_n^{-1} (\bar{\mathbf X}_n-\boldsymbolμ_0). \] Under $H_0$, we establish finite-sample Cramér-type moderate deviation results and uniform Berry--Esseen bounds under finite $p$th moments for $2<p\le3$. The moderate deviation error order is optimal over independent triangular arrays, as shown by explicit constructions. For identically distributed observations with a fixed distribution, we obtain \[ \sup_{0\le x\le b_n} \left| \frac{\mathbb P(T^2_{H,n}\ge x^2)} {\mathbb P(χ_d^2\ge x^2)}-1 \right| = O\!\left((1+b_n)^p n^{-(p-2)/2}\right) \] for every nonnegative sequence $b_n=o(n^{(p-2)/(2p)})$. The uniform Berry--Esseen bound is $O(n^{-(p-2)/2})$. The proof uses a radial Stein identity and a recursive error estimate. We apply the results to chi-squared calibration in simultaneous testing.

items.title: On some stochastic evolutions on Laguerre-Polya functions
items.summary: We prove uniqueness in law for three stochastic evolutions on normalised Laguerre-Pólya functions arising as scaling limits of matrix characteristic polynomial dynamics. In particular, this implies that Ahn's universal Brownian Gibbs line ensemble arising from random matrix products has the law of the logarithms of the reciprocal zeros of the solution, unique in law, to a simple stochastic equation on entire functions started from $\mathrm{e}^{-z}$. The method of proof relies on some integrable structure of the problem in the special form of a new duality with finite-dimensional diffusions which is closely related to intertwinings.

items.title: Undecidability in Relevant Logic
items.summary: We prove undecidability for every positive relevant logic extending the system axiomatized by hypothetical syllogism, prefixing, and suffixing and contained in the logic of the semilattice frame $(P_{\mathrm{fin}}(\mathbb{N}), \cup, \varnothing)$. This settles the longstanding decision problem for the semilattice relevant logic S in the negative, contrary to prevailing expectations of decidability. It also provides a new proof of Urquhart's (1984) undecidability theorem for R, E, and T, now by reduction from the Wang tiling problem for arbitrarily large finite isosceles right triangular regions of the plane.

items.title: Reduction of Zieve's Conjecture on the Hurwitz problem to Three Branch Points
items.summary: M. E. Zieve conjectured that a candidate datum over the sphere is realizable whenever the gcd of the parts of every branch partition is one and it satisfies the lcm condition. We prove that this conjecture reduces to its three-branch-point case. More precisely, if every Zieve-admissible triple is realizable, then every Zieve-admissible datum with at least four branch points is realizable. As already noted by Petronio, Zieve's conjecture would imply the prime-degree conjecture of Edmonds, Kulkarni, and Stong. Song, Wen, and Zhang proved the latter conjecture in a preprint posted on arXiv in September.

items.title: Diameter bounds for complexes that are close to flag or close to normal
items.summary: The Hirsch problem asks how large the diameter of the dual graph of a simplicial complex can be, in terms of its number of vertices. For normal complexes, the classical bounds are the Larman-Barnette bound, which is linear for fixed dimension, the Kalai-Kleitman bound, which is quasi-polynomial, and the Adiprasito-Benedetti bound n-d, which however holds only for flag complexes. After sharpening the Larman-Barnette and the Kalai-Kleitman bounds, we study how the three bounds deteriorate when flagness or normality is weakened. We give three ways to quantify the distance from flagness, and in each case we bound the diameter in a way that interpolates between the Adiprasito-Benedetti and the Larman-Barnette bounds. We also quantify the distance from normality by a parameter q, and obtain a bound that is a polynomial of degree q in n. Finally, we conjecture a statement on flag layered families that would imply an interpolation between the Adiprasito-Benedetti and the Kalai-Kleitman bounds.

items.title: Biharmonic surfaces with flat normal bundle in the four-dimensional sphere
items.summary: We prove that a proper biharmonic surface with flat normal bundle in the four-dimensional unit sphere $\mathbb S^4$ lies minimally in a small hypersphere of radius $1/\sqrt{2}$. Since the surfaces with constant mean curvature and those with parallel normalized mean curvature vector field are already understood, the core of the paper is the non-existence of biharmonic surfaces with flat normal bundle in $\mathbb S^4$ whose mean curvature is not constant and whose normalized mean curvature vector field is not parallel. We first show, adapting an argument of Fu, Hong and Yang, that the gradient of the mean curvature is a principal direction. Then the problem reduces to a first order system of ordinary differential equations with a constraint, and we show that this system has no admissible solutions by an elimination argument.

items.title: Torsion points on $\rm{GL}_2$-type abelian varieties
items.summary: It is well known that the order of the torsion group of an abelian variety over a number field divides the greatest common divisor of the sizes of points on the reduction at each prime (except for an explicit finite set). Drawing inspiration from Katz's Inventiones paper (1981), we investigate the converse to this for abelian varieties of \(\rm GL_2\)-type and exhibit a tentative list of possible rational torsion orders for modular abelian varieties over \(\mathbb Q\) of dimension up to \(5\).

items.title: The universal property of the decomposition space of quasisymmetric functions
items.summary: Aguiar, Bergeron, and Sottile showed that the coalgebra of quasisymmetric functions is terminal among connected graded coalgebras with a zeta function. After developing the notions of gradings and zeta functions for decomposition spaces, we establish an objective homotopic version of this result. Namely, the decomposition space $Q$ of quasisymmetric functions is terminal: for any conservatively graded decomposition space $X$ with zeta function $F$, there is a unique graded ikeo-culf span $X \leftarrow W \rightarrow Q$ inducing $F$ from the special zeta function on $Q$. More generally, for gradings in any complete decomposition space $M$ with indecomposable identities, the terminal object is $J(M)$, the free decomposition space on the nondegenerate simplices of $M$; the quasisymmetric case is $Q=J(B\mathbb{N})$.

items.title: A globally convergent stochastic semismooth Newton method for strongly convex problems in Hilbert spaces
items.summary: We propose and analyze a globalized stochastic semismooth Newton method for stochastic optimization problems in Hilbert spaces where the objective is strongly convex with Lipschitz continuous, Newton differentiable gradient. Gradient and generalized Hessian information are only available through mini-batching. In each iteration, a full semismooth Newton trial step is accepted or rejected based on a stochastic residual test and rejected steps are replaced by damped steps in the same Newton direction. Throughout, we admit gradient estimators with affinely growing variance, as arises in optimization problems with random partial differential equations as constraints. We prove non-asymptotic global R-linear convergence in expectation as well as almost sure convergence. For sufficiently fast-growing batch sizes, the method transitions almost surely into a regime of pure Newton steps and converges R-superlinearly almost surely. The method is applied to the optimal control of a random elliptic equation featuring a Huber tracking term as well as a random parabolic equation with a Moreau--Yosida penalization of an almost sure state constraint.

items.title: Non-Archimedean balanced metrics and their application to totally degenerate abelian varieties
items.summary: For a polarized complex manifold with discrete automorphism group, it is known that if the first Chern class admits a cscK metric, then the balanced metrics, which are characterized in terms of the algebro-geometric notion of Chow stability, approximate this cscK metric. In this paper, we study a non-Archimedean analogue of this phenomenon. In particular, we prove that such an analogue holds for polarized totally degenerate abelian varieties. As an application, we also show that, for a totally degenerating family of polarized abelian varieties, the validity of this non-Archimedean analogue yields a uniform estimate for the Calabi--Yau metrics on fibers sufficiently close to the degenerate fiber.

items.title: Closed-form solution for semi-symmetric folding of waterbomb tessellations
items.summary: Rigid-origami folding has versatile applications in the fields of architecture, engineering, medicine and aerospace. Given the design parameters of a single waterbomb cell, the global geometry of the origami tessellated shell at an intermediate state of folding is directly determined. Even though existing numerical methods of rigid-origami can be used to describe geometric forms, algebraic solutions of the waterbomb folding kinematics and tessellations reduce the algorithmic complexity and determine the range of admissible configurations exactly. The existing analytical solution for a symmetrically folded waterbomb cell and tessellation is extended to the case of a cell folded semi-symmetrically, i.e. a cell with a 180° rotation symmetry. The algebraic derivation provides the solution for the entire folding process. The resulting functional relationship between the design parameters and the 3D cell geometry of the folded waterbomb cell enables efficient studies of achievable shell geometries. This development facilitates a deeper understanding of the correspondence between the geometric parameters of a single waterbomb cell and the statically relevant geometric properties, i.e. the shell curvature and the effective cross-sectional height. The systematic description of this correspondence provides the basis for innovative design concepts using modern cementitious composites, e.g. textile-reinforced concrete, to produce thin-walled, high-performance, lightweight shells.

items.title: Bounds for the univalent Bloch-Landau constant
items.summary: The univalent Bloch-Landau constant $\mathcal{U}$ is the largest number such that, for every univalent function $f$ on the unit disk, $f(\mathbb{D})$ contains a disk of radius $\mathcal{U}|f'(0)|$. We prove $0.619\le\mathcal{U}<0.6562681$. The previous lower bound, $0.57088586$, came from growth estimates, which control disks centered at $f(0)$, and we show that for Landau-normalized functions such disks cannot give a bound above $0.6$. The main new idea is to move the center of the disk.
