After Landau's normalization, a compression of the Grunsky matrix constrains every omitted value through the same few coefficients, so a center chosen from these coefficients can be kept away from all omitted values at once. A short analytic proof based on this idea gives $\mathcal{U}\ge0.592$, and a three-row compression, together with pointwise consequences of Landau's normalization, improves the lower bound to $\mathcal{U}\ge0.619$ through an interval certificate. For the upper bound, we construct an explicit domain, bounded by Goodman's first two slit generations, thirty analytic arcs and a circle. We certify $\mathcal{U}<0.6562681$ with a capacity estimate for almost critical arcs, improving the best published bound $0.6563937$.

items.title: Homogeneous linearly ordered spaces
items.summary: Every compact subspace $K$ of a homogeneous generalized ordered (GO) space $X$ satisfies $χ(K)\leqω_1$ and $|K|\leq 2^{ω_1}$. If $χ(K)>ω$ for some such $K$, then $χ(X)=ω_1$ and $πχ(X)=ω$. We construct a homogeneous $σ$-compact linearly ordered topological space (LOTS) $\mathbf{H}$ with a compact subspace $K$ such that $χ(x,K)=ω_1$ for every $x\in K$ and $c(K)=w(K)=|K|=2^{ω_1}$, where $c(K)$ denotes cellularity. Thus both bounds are attained by the same compact space. Every semitopological group that is a GO space is hereditarily paracompact and has metrizable compact subspaces. If it is not a $P$-space, it is also first countable and submetrizable. A semitopological group that is a LOTS, or a topological group that is a GO space, is either metrizable or is a $P$-space. We also show that in an order-homogeneous LOTS every compact subset is first countable.

items.title: An elementary proof of a tangent-cone identity for rank-one planar Lipschitz maps
items.summary: We give an elementary proof of a tangent-cone identity which might be known to specialists in geometric measure theory. It concerns Lipschitz mappings $g$ from the closed unit ball $B\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ to $\mathbb{R}^2$. Let $x$ be an interior point of differentiability of $g$ at which $Dg(x)$ has rank one. If the upper one-dimensional Hausdorff density of $g(B)$ at $g(x)$ is at most one, then the tangent cone to $g(B)$ at $g(x)$ coincides with the image of $Dg(x)$. This property is used in the proof of rigidity for the four-gradient problem. We provide a detailed, self-contained proof based on differentiability, connectedness and elementary estimates for one-dimensional Hausdorff measure, without using advanced methods from geometric measure theory.

items.title: On Grassmann $4$-designs
items.summary: We prove that there is a unique tight $4$-design in the real Grassmannian $G_{2,4}$, up to the action of $O(4)$. Using symmetric association schemes, we also construct an $N$-point $4$-design in $G_{2,4}$ for every even integer $N\geq10$. For symmetric association schemes of order less than $21$, we classify the pairs of rank-three primitive idempotents defining injective maps into $G_{2,4}$; their images are Grassmannian $4$-designs precisely for four schemes of order $16$.

items.title: Few-Weight Linear Sets and Divisibility of Rank-Metric Codes
items.summary: We study $\mathbb F_q$-linear sets whose positive point weights belong to a prescribed finite set $A$. The integer $e=\gcd(A)$ always divides the rank of the defining subspace, but the divisibility does not by itself imply linearity over $\mathbb F_{q^e}$. We show that it does in a broad parameter range. Let $L_U$ be an $\mathbb F_q$-linear set of rank $N$ spanning $PG(h-1,q^m)$, $h\ge2$, without being equal to it, and assume that $q\ge m$ and that the minimum weight of its points is $a\ge2$. Combining the theorem of Csajbók, Marino and Pepe on the maximum field of linearity with the lower bound of Adriaensen and Santonastaso for the size of a linear set containing a point of weight one, we prove that $L_U$ is also defined by an $\mathbb F_{q^t}$-subspace, for some divisor $t$ of $m$, whose $\mathbb F_q$-dimension is exactly $N+t-a$. Under a natural gap condition excluding divisors of $m$ in the interval $(e,N-e]$, this forces $a=e$ and the defining subspace to be $\mathbb F_{q^e}$-linear. Through geometric duality, the point weights of the dual of a system are the deficiencies $m-w$ of the rank weights $w$ of the associated code. For rank-metric codes in which the subcode generated by the codewords of nonmaximum rank contains codewords of maximum rank, we show that deleting suitable coordinates yields the $\mathbb F_q$-expansion of a code over $\mathbb F_{q^t}$. We show that the codes in which the codewords of nonmaximum rank generate a subcode without codewords of maximum rank are exactly the direct sums of a simplex code and a code of length smaller than $m$. We derive field-reduction results for two-weight and three-weight rank-metric codes, and show that no gap condition is needed when $m$ divides the length or when the code has only two nonzero weights. Finally, we study two-dimensional codes of length at most $m$ and provide families of three-weight examples.

items.title: The stochastic Ginzburg-Landau equation with harmonic potential in the full subcritical regime
items.summary: In this paper, we construct the complex Ginzburg-Landau dynamic associated with the harmonic oscillator, with a random force which is white in time and covers the full subcritical range in space. We are able to renormalise the non-linearity using the same constant as the one used to renormalise the problem associated to the Laplacian. By an extension of the problem to complex times, we are able to prove that the solution of the complex Ginzburg-Landau is equal in law to the solution of the purely dissipative case, i.e. the associated complex $Φ^4$ model, but along a complex axis of time.

items.title: Recovering the Length of a Path from its Signature
items.summary: We prove the length conjecture of J. Chang, T. Lyons and H. Ni for paths of bounded variation for arbitrary real Banach spaces and any reasonable tensor (algebra) norms. More precisely, we establish the missing lower bound and in this way show that the length of a tree-reduced path is recovered from the asymptotic behaviour of its normalised signature. The main technical argument uses the norm duality and shuffle algebra to express natural powers of polygonal length approximations as combinations of linear functionals acting on restricted signatures, which are then glued by suitable integrations into a linear functional of controlled growth acting on the full signature. In particular, the full proof combines tools of classical analysis and functional analysis, such as localisation by continuous cutoff functions, Stone-Weierstrass approximation of continuous functions by signature polynomials, the Hahn-Banach theorem and a support detection lemma for compactly supported real signed Borel measures.

items.title: On Sufficient Conditions for Rank Zero in Families of Elliptic Curves
items.summary: In this article, we study the Mordell Weil ranks of elliptic curves in the family $E_D:y^2=x^3+Dx$, where $D\in\mathbb{Z}\setminus\{0\}$. Under suitable congruence conditions on $D$ and its prime divisors, we use $2$-descent via a rational $2$-isogeny to study the rank of $E_D$. Under our congruence hypotheses, the ranks of these matrices give sufficient conditions for $E_D$ to have rank zero. We give explicit sufficient conditions for the curves $E_D$ to have Mordell Weil rank zero over $\mathbb{Q}$ in the following cases: (i) $D$ is an odd negative integer, (ii) $D$ is an odd positive integer, and (iii) $D$ is a positive even integer. Also we give a quantitative result describing how many square free parameters satisfy the required matrix-rank condition. In particular, our results show that these rank zero criteria hold for a significant proportion of the admissible parameters.

items.title: Splay ostracism on ferroelectric nematic shells
items.summary: Ostracism was the practice in use in Athens and other ancient Greek cities to send into exile citizens whose influence was deemed to be dangerous. Quite similarly, splay ostracism is here the approximation that bans splay distortion from thin films of ferroelectric nematic liquid crystals on a curved shell in space. This reduces to a mere geometric problem the quest for equilibria of director vortexes and the walls isolating them, as splay ostracism requires the director field lines to be everywhere orthogonal to systems of geodesics on the shell. Consequences of this theorem are explored for shells with Gaussian curvature of either sign. The resulting quasi static dynamics reveals both cases where walls escape from the shell and cases where they are trapped on it, with possibly different reflections on the vortex dynamics.

items.title: Exact regions for the symmetrized Blest coefficient
items.summary: Spearman's rho treats all ranks alike, yet in many comparisons of two rankings an agreement at the top matters more than one at the bottom. Blest's rank correlation builds this preference into Spearman's rho, and its symmetrized version $η$, introduced by Genest and Plante, does so without favoring either of the two rankings. How far can such a top-weighted coefficient stray from other rank correlations? We answer this question for Spearman's rho, Blomqvist's beta and Chatterjee's rank correlation $ξ$ by determining the exact set of values that $η$ and each of these coefficients can attain jointly. Given Spearman's rho, $η$ can differ from it by at most $27/128$, and the extreme values of $η$ are attained only when the two rankings agree perfectly on the top ranks and are completely reversed on the bottom ranks, or vice versa. Given Blomqvist's beta, $η$ obeys exactly the same sharp bounds as Spearman's rho. For Chatterjee's rank correlation, both boundary curves are explicit and are attained by copulas with densities. Here symmetrization has a surprising effect. Compared with Blest's original coefficient, $η$ has a narrower range at fixed Spearman's rho, but near independence a wider range at fixed Chatterjee's rank correlation, where $|η|$ can come close to $\sqrt{11ξ/5}$ while Blest's coefficient stays below $\sqrt{32ξ/15}$. The proofs combine explicit Kantorovich potentials from optimal transport with a convex relaxation that turns out to be exact.

items.title: Fully nonlinear second-order mean field games with nondifferentiable Hamiltonians
items.summary: We analyse fully nonlinear second-order mean field games (MFG) with nondifferentiable Hamiltonians, which take the form of a coupled system of a fully nonlinear Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman equation and a Kolmogorov--Fokker--Planck partial differential inclusion (PDI) featuring the set-valued subdifferential of the Hamiltonian. We show the existence of solutions of some stationary MFG systems with quite general coupling operators and nonnegative distributional source terms, on general bounded convex domains, under the primary assumptions of uniform ellipticity and the Cordes condition on the diffusion coefficient. The existence proof is founded on an original, and equivalent, reformulation of the PDI as a nonstandard variational inequality (VI), that offers significant flexibility in passages to limits. Furthermore, the uniqueness of the solution of the PDI/VI system is proved in the case of strictly monotone couplings. We then show how the MFG PDI/VI system in the fully nonlinear setting can be obtained as the limit of a sequence of PDE systems with differentiable Hamiltonians, and we give further results on the continuous dependence of the solution.

items.title: Random Cayley sum hypergraphs and $k$-fold sumsets
items.summary: We denote by $f_k(Γ)$ the largest integer with the property that every subset of a finite abelian group $Γ$ of size at least $|Γ| - f_k(Γ)$ is a $k$-fold sumset. Extending a recent result of Alon and Pham, we prove that $$ f_k(Γ) \leq \widetilde{O} \left(n^{(2k-1)/(4k-3)}\right) $$ holds for all finite abelian groups $Γ$ and integers $k \geq 2$, where $n = |Γ|$. Additionally, we also show that the lower bound $f_k(Γ) \geq \widetildeΩ \left(n^{1/k}\right)$ holds if $Γ$ has no nontrivial element of order dividing $k$. Our upper bound improves a previous result of Balogh, Liu, and Sharifzadeh, and recovers the bound of Alon and Pham in the case $k = 2$. The proof relies on a new upper bound for the independence number of random Cayley sum hypergraphs, which may be of independent interest.

items.title: Domination and maximal intersecting families in comaximal graphs of commutative rings
items.summary: The comaximal graph $\mathcal{G}(R)$ of a commutative ring $R$ has as vertices the nonunits outside the Jacobson radical, two being adjacent if they generate $R$ as an ideal. For rings with $k\ge 4$ maximal ideals, only the bounds $2\leγ(\mathcal{G}(R))\le k$ were known, to our knowledge. We prove $γ=γ_t=γ_c=k$ whenever $3\le k<\infty$, without finiteness or Artinian hypotheses, classify the minimum dominating sets, and determine the domatic number. Independent dominating sets correspond to maximal intersecting families of subsets of $\{1,\dots,k\}$; we obtain a closed formula for the independent domination number of every finite non-local ring, which can be exponentially larger than the domination number. The proofs rest on the class sizes of the blow-up description of $\mathcal{G}(R)$ due to Moconja and Petrović, which we determine for every ring with finitely many maximal ideals, finite or infinite; with them, domination problems on $\mathcal{G}(R)$ become weighted extremal problems on subsets of $\{1,\dots,k\}$, and the formula for the independent domination number follows from the multiplicative form of these sizes. We also treat rings with infinitely many maximal ideals, graph polynomials, and lattices whose maximal ideals are prime.

items.title: Weighted Robin eigenvalue problems and nonlinear elliptic equations with general growth in the gradient
items.summary: We prove an existence result for Robin boundary value problems modeled on \[ \begin{cases} Δu + |\nabla u|^2 + λf(x) = 0 & \text{in } Ω \\ \frac{\partial u}{\partial ν} + βu = 0 & \text{on } \partialΩ\end{cases} \] where $Ω$ is a bounded, sufficiently smooth open set in $\mathbb R^N$, $f(x)$ belongs to the Marcinkiewicz space $M^{\frac N2}$ and {$β>0$}, under a smallness assumption on the datum $λ$. In order to study such problem, we will show several properties of the weighted, singular Robin eigenvalue problem \[ λ_{1,f,γ}(Ω)= \inf_{ψ\in H^{1},\;\int_Ωfψ^{2}=1}\left\{\int_Ω|\nabla ψ|^{2}dx+γ\int_{\partialΩ}ψ^{2}\right\}. \]

items.title: Sigmoid Tensor Decomposition for Compact Representations of Binary Data
items.summary: Nonlinear low-rank decompositions are receiving growing attention as a way to represent structured data with fewer parameters than conventional linear methods. Existing nonlinear approaches have focused mainly on matrices, which limits their ability to capture multidimensional structure. We propose a nonlinear tensor decomposition based on sigmoid nonlinearization in the Tucker and tensor-train formats. A binary tensor is represented by a low-rank real-valued score tensor, whose parameters are estimated by minimizing the binary cross-entropy loss. The resulting optimization problem is jointly nonconvex, but becomes convex with respect to one factor or score block when the remaining factors are fixed, as in the corresponding matrix case. We evaluate the method on several structured binary tensors and compare it with conventional Tucker and tensor-train decompositions across a range of common ranks. These results indicate that sigmoid nonlinearization is particularly effective in the low-rank regime, where it can provide more accurate binary reconstructions than conventional linear tensor decompositions at comparable model sizes.

items.title: Universal $x$-$y$ duality in equivariant topological recursion and quartic Kontsevich model
items.summary: Topological recursion is a universal procedure that generates an infinite family of multi-differentials with different interpretations in various areas of mathematics. Recently, a new understanding of topological recursion has emerged from $x$-$y$ duality, which relates two such families through explicit formulae. We study $x$-$y$ duality, its parametrised version, and symplectic duality in the setting of equivariant topological recursion. We explicitly analyse the pole structure of the resulting dual families and provide recursive formulae for the different types of polar parts. In contrast to classical topological recursion, the dual family has additional poles at fixed points of the group action, and at anti-diagonals determined by the group action. We show that the partition function $Z_P(E)=\int_{H_N} e^{-N\,\mathrm{Tr}(EΦ^2+P(Φ))}dΦ$ of the Kontsevich matrix model with arbitrary potential $P$, where $dΦ$ is the Lebesgue measure on Hermitian $N\times N$ matrices and $E$ a positive matrix, admits a Fock space realisation related to the character expansion of the IZHC integral. The Fock space framework provides two mutually $X$-$Y$ dual families of multi-differentials relative to an implicitly defined spectral curve $(X,Y)$. The solution $Y(X)$ succeeds for the quartic Kontsevich model with potential $P(Φ)=\fracλ{4}Φ^4$. We identify a network of duality transformations and symplectic shifts which relate the quartic Kontsevich model with the $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$-equivariant spectral curve. The proposed construction yields a conjectural all-genus solution to the quartic Kontsevich model, which reproduces recursive structures previously established for genus $g\leq 1$.

items.title: The Modified Camassa--Holm Equation with Step-Like Boundary Conditions: A Characterization of Existence
items.summary: We consider the Cauchy problem for the modified Camassa-Holm equation \[ u_t+\left((u^2-u_x^2)m\right)_x=0,\quad m:= u-u_{xx}, \quad t>0,\ \ -\infty<x<+\infty \] subject to the step-like initial data: $u(x,0)\to A_1$ as $x\to-\infty$ and $u(x,0)\to A_2$ as $x\to+\infty$, where $0<A_1<A_2$. First, using the Riemann--Hilbert approach, we establish the global solvability of the corresponding problem in the reciprocal $(y,t)$-variables. Then the reconstruction in the original $(x,t)$-variables is obtained under a positivity condition expressed in terms of the solution of the associated Riemann--Hilbert problem.

items.title: Funnel MPC for port-Hamiltonian systems
items.summary: Port-Hamiltonian systems are an energy-based modelling formalism, that has strong ties to the physical models and allows interconnection of systems. Funnel MPC, a Model Predictive Control (MPC) scheme, allows for output tracking with prescribed error bounds. Earlier works focused on systems with stable internal dynamics, which typically excludes port-Hamiltonian systems. We introduce a modified stage cost design that takes into account the port-Hamiltonian structure of the system and allows deactivation of the funnel cost. We show initial and recursive feasibility for a class of port-Hamiltonian systems with relative degree one including unstable internal dynamics.

items.title: Sharp Finiteness Principles for the boundary values of $C^2$-functions
items.summary: Let $Ω$ be an arbitrary domain in ${\bf R}^n$, and let $C^2(Ω)$ be the space of all functions whose partial derivatives of all orders up to two are continuous and bounded on $Ω$. We prove the following Finiteness Principle for the boundary values of $C^2(Ω)$-functions: A function $f$ defined on the boundary of $Ω$ is the trace of a function $F\in C^2(Ω)$ provided there exists $λ>0$ such that, for every set $E$ of at most $N=3\cdot 2^{n-1}$ boundary points, there exists a function $F_E\in C^2(Ω)$ with $\|F_E\|_{C^2(Ω)}\leλ$ whose trace coincides with $f$ on $E$. Moreover, $F$ can be chosen with $\|F\|_{C^2(Ω)}\leγλ$ where $γ$ depends only on $n$. We also refine this principle by showing that it suffices to consider $N$-point sets $E$ with specific geometric ``visibility'' properties relative to $Ω$.

items.title: A blow-up approach for a priori bounds in semilinear planar elliptic systems: the Brezis-Merle critical case
items.summary: We establish uniform a priori estimates for solutions of semilinear planar Hamiltonian elliptic systems in a ball with Dirichlet boundary conditions. We consider a broad class of coupled nonlinearities with asymptotic critical behaviour in the sense of Brezis--Merle. The approach we follow is based on a blow-up analysis combined with Liouville--type theorems and integral estimates. Our results extend the scalar theory of uniform a priori bounds to the Hamiltonian case, and solve an open problem in [de Figueiredo D.G., do Ó J.M., Ruf B., Adv. Nonlinear Stud. 6 (2006), no. 2]. We believe that this approach is new in this setting. As a consequence of our a priori estimates, we prove the existence of a positive solution by means of fixed-point index theory.

items.title: Generalized Hopf bifurcations: a homological analysis and obstructions to their existence
items.summary: A generalized Hopf bifurcation takes place when varying a parameter of a (semi)dynamical system causes an attractor $K$ to become a repeller. In doing so, it expels a (parameter-dependent) family of attractors. In this paper we concentrate on two questions: (1) what do the expelled attractors look like?, and (2) can any attractor $K$ undergo a generalized Hopf bifurcation? Regarding (1), we compute the cohomology of the expelled attractors in terms of the cohomology of $K$; in the case of continuous-time dynamics this can be improved to a computation of their Borsuk shape. As for (2), we show that certain compacta cannot undergo generalized Hopf bifurcations and, when the ambient space has dimension $ \leq 3$, give a complete topological characterization of which can.

items.title: LithoSAGE: Spatially Adaptive and Geometrically Equivariant Neural Operators for Computational Lithography
items.summary: Operator learning offers an efficient surrogate for lithography simulation, replacing costly numerical solutions with direct model inference. However, existing learning architectures are not designed to simultaneously provide geometric equivariance and adaptability to layout windows with different physical extents, and thus their generalization capability is limited. To address this problem, we propose LithoSAGE, a spatially adaptive and geometrically equivariant neural operator method trained on lithography data. Within its basic Fourier neural operator architecture, spectral weights are expressed as continuous functions of normalized radial frequency through a learnable sum of Gaussians. This representation preserves the geometric properties of the lithography system and incorporates rotation and translation equivariance, spatial interaction decay, and direct evaluation on different layout windows. Experiments predict aerial images from mask layouts and resist images from aerial images, demonstrating the geometric equivariance and spatial adaptivity of LithoSAGE. Comparisons with other architectures also assess prediction errors and parameter efficiency.

items.title: Hypocoercivity for a thermostatted Boltzmann equation
items.summary: We study the Boltzmann equation for a gas on the three-dimensional torus. Its particles collide with one another and with a thermal reservoir whose temperature varies in space. The reservoir heats the gas in some regions and cools it in others, driving a nonequilibrium energy current. For the isotropic cutoff kernel, with Maxwell molecules or hard potentials, we prove global well-posedness and exponential convergence to the same stationary state for initial data with a common Gaussian upper bound and Gaussian moment bound. These bounds determine how weak self collisions must be relative to bath collisions. The estimates are uniform over bath profiles between fixed positive temperature bounds. For any nonconstant reservoir profile on the three-dimensional torus, this stationary state cannot be a local Maxwellian. When particles collide only with the bath, relative entropy to the stationary state cannot increase. Once self collisions are added, arbitrarily small perturbations can initially increase it, even though they later return exponentially.

items.title: On a generalized Monge-Ampère equation on closed almost Kähler surfaces
items.summary: We show the existence and uniqueness of solutions to a generalized Monge-Ampère equation on closed almost Kähler surfaces, where the equation depends only on the underlying almost Kähler structure. As an application, we prove Donaldson's conjecture for tamed almost complex 4-manifolds.

items.title: Mutual-visibility k-colouring is NP-complete for every fixed diameter
items.summary: A mutual-visibility set in a graph G is a set S of vertices such that any two vertices of S are connected by a shortest path with no internal vertex in S, and the mutual-visibility chromatic number $χ_μ(G)$ is the minimum number of mutual-visibility sets needed to partition V(G). Babu, Di Stefano and Lakshmanan showed that it is NP-complete to decide whether $χ_μ(G)\le 2$ for graphs of diameter four. We show that the problem remains NP-complete for graphs of diameter d, for every fixed $d\ge2$; diameter two is the smallest diameter for which the problem is non-trivial. More generally, for all fixed $k\ge2$ and $d\ge2$, it is NP-complete to decide whether $χ_μ(G)\le k$ for graphs of diameter d. The proof rests on a reformulation of $χ_μ(G)\le 2$ for diameter-two graphs as the 2-colourability of an associated hypergraph, and on a reduction from 2-colourability of 3-uniform hypergraphs without short cycles.

items.title: Isomorphisms and automorphisms of minimal comaximal hypergraphs of commutative rings
items.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative ring with exactly $n\ge 2$ maximal ideals and let $k\ge 2$. We study the minimal $k$-uniform comaximal hypergraph $\mathcal{H}_k(R)$, whose vertices are the nonunits outside the Jacobson radical and whose edges are the irredundant $k$-element comaximal families. For $2\le k\le n$ we show that $\mathcal{H}_k(R)$ is a blow-up of the hypergraph of irredundant $k$-coverings of $\{1,\dots,n\}$, and that its reduced form reconstructs the maximal ideals up to permutation; for $k>n$ there are no edges. We obtain a general description of $\mathrm{Aut}(\mathcal{H}_k(R))$ and characterize isomorphisms of such hypergraphs. For $3\le k\le n$ its automorphism group properly contains that of the comaximal graph, and for finite rings with $n\ge 3$ and every $2\le k\le n$, $\mathcal{H}_k(R)$ has the same isomorphism invariants as the comaximal graph, namely $|J(R)|$ and $R/J(R)$. The case $k=2$ recovers and extends the automorphism results for comaximal graphs obtained previously. We also compare the minimal and non-minimal comaximal hypergraphs and identify a condition under which the latter has the same automorphism group and isomorphism invariants as the comaximal graph. The same method determines the vertex set and the automorphism group of the $k$-zero-divisor hypergraph of a product of integral domains, and shows that for finite products of finite fields this hypergraph determines the ring.

items.title: Parameter-dependent inhomogeneous boundary-value problems in spaces of continuously differentiable functions
items.summary: We investigate a broad class of linear inhomogeneous boundary-value problems of order $r$ for systems of ordinary differential equations depending on a parameter $μ$ belonging to an abstract metric space $\mathcal M$. The solutions belong to the spaces of continuously differentiable vector-valued functions $(C^{(n+r)})^m$, $n\in\mathbb{N}\cup\{0\}$, $m, r \in \mathbb{N}$. The boundary conditions have the most general form $By=c$, where $B$ is an arbitrary continuous linear operator from $(C^{(n+r)})^m$ to $\mathbb{C}^{rm}$. Thus, they may contain derivatives of the unknown vector-valued function of integer and/or fractional orders up to $n+r$ inclusive. We establish necessary and sufficient conditions for the continuous dependence of solutions on the parameter $μ$. Furthermore, we prove that the solutions of the original problems can be approximated in the space $(C^{(n+r)})^m$ by solutions of systems of ordinary differential equations with polynomial coefficients, polynomial right-hand sides, and multipoint boundary conditions, where the approximating problems are constructed independently of the right-hand sides of the original problem.

items.title: Tilting bundles and modifying modules in relative dimension one
items.summary: For projective morphisms $π:Y\to X=\operatorname{Spec}R$ over noetherian complete local rings, with fibres of dimension at most one and $\mathbf{R}π_*\mathcal{O}_Y\cong\mathcal{O}_X$, we construct a tilting fan from cones of pretilting bundles. Maximal cones parametrize tilting bundles, and facet adjacency encodes irreducible mutation. Completeness in positive rank is equivalent to finiteness of tilting bundles modulo line-bundle twists. For closed fibres that are split ADE highest-root cycles or their Stein contractions, we identify tilting bundles with chambers of restricted affine Tits cones and determine the fan. Over normal Gorenstein complete local domains, reflexive pushforward takes pretilting bundles on normal projective birational models with fibres of dimension at most one and $π^!\mathcal{O}_X\cong\mathcal{O}_Y$ to modifying modules. Pushforwards of canonical tilting bundles recover models as module blowups and detect contractions by additive containment, yielding an Auslander--McKay embedding. The hypersurfaces $R=S[[u,v]]/(uv-f)$, with $S$ a regular complete local ring and $f\in S$ a nonzero nonunit, generalize type $A$ Du Val surfaces and $cA_n$ threefolds to arbitrary dimension. We classify modifying modules by divisor flags and rank-one reflexive twists; flag blowups turn the embedding into an equivalence. If $f$ has $r\ge2$ prime factors counted with multiplicity, reflexive pushforward on any maximal-flag model gives a mutation-preserving surjection from tilting bundles, parametrized by chambers of affine type $\widetilde{A}_{r-1}$, to maximal modifying modules. Its fibres are affine Weyl group orbits determined by repeated factors. All maximal-flag models and maximal modification algebras are derived equivalent. These algebras are noncommutative crepant resolutions exactly when $S/(p)$ is regular for every prime factor $p$ of $f$.

items.title: Boundary-preserving randomized neural network methods for Poisson equations on general two- and three-dimensional domains
items.summary: In this paper, we propose a boundary-preserving randomized neural network method for Poisson equations with Dirichlet boundary conditions in two and three dimensions. A linear lifting imposes the boundary conditions exactly, without balancing penalty weights between interior and boundary residuals. We construct the liftings by generalized barycentric coordinates and transfinite interpolation on convex and nonconvex polygons and polyhedra, and by radial parameterization on star-shaped curved domains. Numerical experiments on different domains show that the proposed method substantially reduces errors compared with the standard randomized neural network method.

items.title: Central simple algebras, Milnor $K$-theory and homogeneous spaces over complete discretely valued fields of dimension 2
items.summary: Let $K$ be a complete discretely valued field of dimension $2$. We prove the following statements on the arithmetic of $K$. - The ``period equals index'' property holds for central simple $K$-algebras. - If $K$ has characteristic $0$, for every prime $p$, every class in the Milnor $\mathrm{K}$-theory modulo $p$ is represented by a symbol. - Serre's Conjecture II holds for the field $K$. That is, for every semisimple and simply connected $K$-group $G$, the set $H^1(K,G)$ is trivial.

items.title: A stability order barrier and SSP bound for Runge--Kutta methods with non-negative coefficients: AI-assisted proofs
items.summary: We prove three results about Runge--Kutta methods with non-negative coefficients. First, every $s$-stage implicit Runge--Kutta method of order at least two has SSP coefficient at most $2s$; the bound is sharp and is attained by a known diagonally implicit method, so full implicitness gives no advantage over DIRK at second order. This extends the second-order DIRK result of Kocsis \& Németh to full coefficient matrices and settles a conjecture of Ketcheson, Macdonald & Gottlieb. These proofs were found with the assistance of AI tools, which uncovered an interesting relationship between the Butcher matrices for SSP methods and phase-type distributions, and led to the proof of the second result: a bound on the SSP coefficient of $s$-stage implicit Runge--Kutta method of order at least three. The third result in this work is a proof that a third-order Runge--Kutta method with entrywise non-negative $A$ and $b$ cannot be algebraically stable. This algebraically intensive proof was also AI-assisted. This paper describes the iterative process of AI-assisted results, and presents an approach that centers human understanding and creativity in the AI-assisted mathematical endeavor.

items.title: A characterization of purely atomic von Neumann algebras
items.summary: Let $M$ be a semifinite von Neumann algebra with a faithful normal semifinite trace $τ$, and let $Φ$ be an Orlicz function. We prove that the noncommutative Orlicz space $L^Φ(M,τ)$ is contained in $M$ if and only if $M$ is purely atomic and there is $δ>0$ such that $τ(e)\geqδ$ for every nonzero projection $e\in M$. We also prove that every left $M$-module map on $L^Φ(M,τ)$ is bounded. As a consequence, a left ideal of $M$ contained in $L^Φ(M,τ)$ and dense in it admits an $M$-invariant algebraic complement if and only if it is equal to $L^Φ(M,τ)$. These results extend a theorem of Fidaleo and Zsidó from $L^2$ to all noncommutative Orlicz spaces.

items.title: More minor summation formulae
items.summary: We prove determinantal-Pfaffian formulae that simultaneously generalise the Pfaffian minor summation formula of Ishikawa and Wakayama and Byun's recent minor summation formula. These formulae are based on factorisation formulae for the determinant of the sum of a skew-symmetric matrix and a rank-1 matrix. Applications include a Cauchy-type identity for skew Schur functions.

items.title: Darboux transformations of linear birth-death processes
items.summary: In a previous paper we characterized the lower-upper (LU) and upper-lower (UL) factorizations of the infinitesimal generator of a possibly nonconservative birth-death process whose Darboux transformations are again generators of birth-death processes. Here we apply these results to several classical models with linear rates and explicitly known spectral measures: the $M/M/\infty$ queue (Charlier polynomials), the linear birth-death processes (Meixner and Laguerre polynomials), and the linear models of Ismail, Letessier and Valent (associated Laguerre polynomials). For each of them we compute the factors in closed form, determine the admissible ranges of the parameters, and describe the rates, spectral measures and orthogonal polynomials of the Darboux-transformed processes.

items.title: Bounds on the maximum denominator of fractional chromatic numbers
items.summary: For a positive rational number $x=p/q$, where $p$ and $q$ are coprime positive integers, let $\operatorname{den}(x)=q$. For a positive integer $n$, let $\operatorname{sd}(n)=\max\{\operatorname{den}(χ_f(G)): |V(G)|=n\}$. Let $D(n)=2^{-n}(n+1)^{(n+1)/2}$. It was proved by Alon, Tuza and Voigt that $\operatorname{sd}(n)\le D(n)$. In this paper, we prove that $\operatorname{sd}(n)\le D(n)n^{-\frac12\log_2 n+\frac14\log_2\log_2 n+O(1)}$ for all sufficiently large $n$. For the lower bound on $\operatorname{sd}(n)$, it was recently proved by Bonamy, Hylasová, Kaiser and Sereni that $\limsup_{n\to\infty}\operatorname{sd}(n)^{1/n}\ge\sqrt{2}$. We prove that $\limsup_{n\to\infty}\operatorname{sd}(n)^{1/n}\ge 3^{1/3}>\sqrt{2}$.

items.title: A positive answer to Barsotti and Carman's question on unit groups of Burnside rings of fusion systems
items.summary: Let F be a saturated fusion system on a finite 2-group S, and let B(F) be the Burnside ring of F. Barsotti and Carman proved that when S is abelian, B(F)^*=B(S)^* if and only if F=F_S(S). Barsotti and Carman asked on page 728 of their paper whether there exists a counterexample to Corollary 9.3 for a nonabelian 2-group. We have given a positive answer. Our main conclusion is that the following are equivalent for all finite 2-groups: (1)F=F_S(S); (2)B(F)^*=B(S)^*; (3)For every maximal subgroup M of S, 1-[S/M] is in B(F)^*.

items.title: Reversible Dynamics, Asymmetric Actions: Parking as a Trajectory-Level Affordance
items.summary: Drivers are often told to back into a tight parking space, not drive in nose first. The advice looks paradoxical, because a slow car is dynamically reversible: reverse its speed and replay the steering backward, and it retraces a feasible path. Played backward, though, reverse-in shows a car driving forward out of the space. Reverse-in and forward-in are different tasks: they share a start position but end facing opposite ways. We separate three clearances between car and obstacles. Static fit $F$ is the clearance the parked car keeps at its best acceptable destination pose. Eventual access $A_\infty$ is the clearance it can keep all the way there with unlimited corrections. Resource-bounded access $A_K$ is the clearance that survives a budget of $K$ reversals, switches between forward and reverse. They satisfy $F\ge A_\infty\ge A_K$. In one fully specified scene (one car, bay, aisle and start), a certified argument proves $A_\infty=F=0.5000$ m for both tasks. In this scene, all certified forward/reverse asymmetry therefore arises at finite $K$: it lies in how many corrections each task needs, not in the clearance either can eventually keep. With one reversal, an explicit path gives reverse-in at least $0.4410$ m clearance. A certified reachability argument caps forward-in's one-reversal clearance at $d_0<0.1720002$ m. With two reversals, forward-in gets at least $0.2833$ m. To keep a clearance strictly above any $d$ with $d_0\le d<0.2833$ m, reverse-in thus needs exactly one reversal and forward-in exactly two when both tasks move forward first. If both move in reverse first, the counts are two and three. The contrast depends on the start position (Section 4.15). Proposed experiments test whether observers distinguish fit, eventual access and budgeted access. They compare these with simpler cues, such as how the turning body sweeps, and learned manoeuvre labels.

items.title: Multiplicity via symmetry for the Minkowski mean curvature equation: Dirichlet and Neumann problems
items.summary: We consider the Minkowski mean curvature equation $$ -\operatorname{div}\left(\frac{\nabla u}{\sqrt{1-|\nabla u|^2}}\right) =λu+μh(x,u) \quad \text{in } Ω, \quad \mathcal B u = 0 \quad \text{on } \partial Ω, $$ where $\mathcal B \in \{ \mathcal D, \mathcal N \}$ is a Dirichlet or Neumann boundary condition and $Ω$ is a smooth bounded domain, required to be convex in the Neumann case. Moreover, $λ, μ\geq0$ are parameters, and $h(x,u)$ is odd with respect to $u$ and positive for $u > 0$. Using minmax methods in nonsmooth critical point theory, we prove that $λ>λ^\mathcal B_k$ yields at least $k$ pairs of nontrivial solutions with negative energy for every $μ\geq0$, where $λ_k^\mathcal B$ are the corresponding Laplacian eigenvalues, indexed by $λ^\mathcal B_0=0$. Moreover, if $H(x,u):=\int_0^u h(x,t)\,dt=o(u^2)$ as $u\to0$, we prove that for $λ\in[λ^\mathcal B_k,λ^\mathcal B_{k+1})$ and every $j\geq\max\{1,k\}$, sufficiently large $μ$ yields at least $2j-k$ distinct pairs of solutions: $j$ with negative energy and $j-k$ with positive energy.

items.title: The Cone Fixing the Reals of $\mathrm{HOD}^{M_{2n}(x)}$
items.summary: For a cone of reals $x$, the reals of $\mathrm{HOD}^{L[x]}$ are precisely the reals in $Q_3$, or equivalently, the set of reals in $M_1$, the minimal proper class mouse with a Woodin cardinal. We show that if $z$ is any real coding $M_1|δ^{+M_1}$, then $z$ is the base of such a cone (so $M_1^{\#}$ is such a base). We also establish a kind of optimality for this result, by identifying a real $x$ such that $M_1\subseteq L[x]$ but $\mathbb{R}\cap\mathrm{HOD}^{L[x]}\not\subseteq M_1$, although there is a base for the cone in a generic extension of $L[x]$. We prove an analogous result for the reals of $\mathrm{HOD}^{M_{n}(x)}$ for even $n$, as well as an analogous optimality result which holds for all $n$.

items.title: On the Spectral Dependence of Decentralized Stochastic Gradient Tracking
items.summary: We study how the spectral geometry of the mixing matrix enters the convergence of decentralized stochastic gradient tracking (GT) for smooth strongly convex problems. General bounds contain the factor $Δ_λ^{-3}$ in the higher-order stochastic term, where $Δ_λ$ is the absolute spectral gap. We show that, even for two agents with identical quadratic objectives, the exact steady-state mean-square disagreement scales as $α^2σ^2Δ_λ^{-3}$ as the nontrivial eigenvalue approaches $-1$, provided the stepsize $α$ is sufficiently small relative to the gap. Here $σ^2$ is the gradient-noise variance. By unrolling the disagreement recursion, we establish a stochastic bound that averages all nontrivial eigenvalue contributions for diagonalizable mixing matrices, up to an eigenvector conditioning factor. As a real or complex eigenvalue approaches the unit circle away from $1$, its contribution grows as the inverse cube of its distance to the circle; growth can be slower near $1$. For symmetric mixing with gaps $p$ at $1$ and $ν$ at $-1$, the weighted sum $θ_1/p+θ_2/ν^3$ replaces the prior factor $(Δ_λν^2)^{-1}$. For $N$ agents, $Nθ_1$ and $Nθ_2$ count the nonnegative and negative nontrivial eigenvalues, respectively. On a symmetric family, a finite-horizon lower bound for the average iterate matches the worst-case factor $p^{-1}+ν^{-3}$ up to universal constants. Numerical experiments confirm the predicted scaling.

items.title: A fully discrete LBRFD-IPDG method for linear fourth-order parabolic equations
items.summary: We propose a fully discrete method for linear fourth-order parabolic equations with Dirichlet boundary conditions, combining an implicit LBRFD multistep scheme in time with a mixed interior penalty discontinuous Galerkin (IPDG) method in space. The temporal discretization employs equispaced linear barycentric rational interpolants and incorporates a startup procedure. To facilitate the spatial discretization, the original problem is reformulated through an auxiliary variable. For certain parameter pairs $(n,d)$, the LBRFD method is shown to be $A(α)$-stable and to possess a wider stability angle than the corresponding BDF$p$ method of the same order. Stability and a priori error estimates are established via a $G$-energy technique and the discrete Grönwall lemma. The theoretical analysis yields a total $L^2$ error estimate of order $h^{k-1}+τ^p$, where $p=d$ if $n-d$ is even and $p=d+1$ if $n-d$ is odd. The reduced spatial convergence rate is attributed to boundary contributions on $\partialΩ$. Despite this theoretical prediction, numerical experiments confirm the stability and demonstrate optimal convergence of order $h^{k+1}+τ^p$.

items.title: A Note on the Cut-Locus-Corrected Fréchet Mean Central Limit Theorem
items.summary: We record two observations concerning \cite{HLW24}. First, the proof of its Theorem~1 yields the population linearization (13)--(14) at \textit{any critical point} of the Fréchet function $F_μ$, under its remaining geometric and measure-theoretic assumptions; neither isolation nor a nonsingular Hessian of $F_μ$ is needed. Second, its Theorem~2 is given a shorter proof by applying the M-estimator theorem \cite[Theorem~5.23, pp.~53--54]{vdV98} to negative squared distance in normal coordinates, as opposed to the Donsker argument used there. We verify the pointwise differentiability, local square-integrable Lipschitz bound, second order expansion of population loss, consistency, and empirical maximization hypotheses. The resulting covariance retains the cut-locus correction. The same argument applies to suitably selected local sample Fréchet minima when the population Hessian is positive definite.

items.title: Constructive Probability, Foundations and Numerical Analysis for mathematical finance and machine learning
items.summary: This monograph sets out a constructive theory of stochastic processes in the continuum, in the sense of constructive field theory: the continuum is not postulated but reached as the limit of a sequence of lattice approximations, with the renormalisation the limit requires exhibited rather than assumed, and the limit controlled by estimates that can be checked. The primitive object is not a sigma-algebra but de Finetti's prevision, the price of finitely many gambles at a fixed resolution, which coherence turns into a conditional expectation. The theorem at the centre of the book, called plainly the fundamental theorem, is at once de Finetti's fundamental theorem of probability, the fundamental theorem of Bayesian statistics, and the one-period fundamental theorem of asset pricing; the financial vocabulary is a convenience only. The applications are two, mathematical finance and machine learning, and they are one mathematics read in opposite directions: an assessment is a price in the one and a prediction in the other, and both are computed by one adjoint recursion, the adjoint of a propagation in the first case and backpropagation in the second. Carried through, the two directions give sharp rates of convergence rather than asymptotic orders: for the moments of Ito diffusions, for the value function of Feynman-Kac semigroups, and for the measure changes of the fundamental theorem, the last as a limit theorem for reweighted generators, under a condition keeping the reweighting well behaved. A measure change is thus calculated, not postulated: a lattice approximation with Farkas' lemma computes it, completeness makes it unique, and the passage to the continuum is earned by the regularity of what is computed. Sixty-seven Python scripts regenerate every numerical table, and much of the finite-dimensional core of the argument has been verified in Lean 4.

items.title: P-curvature from a TQFT viewpoint
items.summary: This paper is motivated by the recent discovery, in symplectic topology, of a relation (partly proved, partly conjectural) between quantum connection and quantum Steenrod operations. We introduce an abstract TQFT framework, based on certain features of the definition of deformed symplectic cohomology, in which such a relation holds generally.

items.title: The Approximation Property without the Bounded Approximation Property in a Separable Banach Space and Its Dual
items.summary: We investigate whether a dual Banach space with the approximation property (AP) must necessarily have the bounded approximation property (BAP). Using a quantitative renorming theorem for the space of absolutely summable sequences, we establish a direct-sum construction yielding a negative answer. More precisely, we construct a separable Banach space (X) such that both (X) and its dual (X^*) have the approximation property, while neither space has the bounded approximation property. The construction uses a sequence of equivalent renormings of (\ell_1) with increasingly restrictive finite-dimensional approximation bounds. By assembling these spaces through a (c_0)-direct sum, we obtain a dual space whose approximation property is preserved, but whose approximation constants cannot be uniformly bounded. We establish the required transfer principles, including the preservation of approximation bounds under complemented coordinate projections and the descent of the bounded approximation property from a dual space to its predual. We also provide an explicit complex-scalar version of the construction. The argument separates the external quantitative renorming input from the direct-sum construction and its functional-analytic consequences. In particular, the resulting example demonstrates that the approximation property of a dual space does not imply its bounded approximation property, even when the predual is separable and both spaces possess the approximation property.

items.title: Kobayashi hyperbolicity of complete linear systems on abelian varieties
items.summary: We provide a geometric condition ensuring that a very general element of a complete linear system on an abelian variety is Kobayashi hyperbolic. This can be seen as the counterpart of some classical results on very general hypersurfaces in projective spaces. Some related conjectures are also given, and involve a natural constant, the so-called basepoint-freeness threshold, associated with any polarized abelian variety $(A, L)$ detecting information about the hyperbolicity of $|L|$.

items.title: A Story of Algebra and Categories I: Algebraic Theories
items.summary: This is the first part of a series of expository notes on homotopical and categorical algebra. It charts a course from ordinary algebraic structures such as monoids, groups, and rings to their various homotopy-coherent generalizations and equivariant versions. The emphasis is on the ideas that lead to and connect the constructions, as well as where and how they appear in nature.

items.title: Clique partitions and distinct color sets in list colorings
items.summary: For an \(n\)-vertex graph \(G\) and an integer \(m\ge n\), let \(f'(G,m)\) be the minimum number of distinct color sets used by proper colorings from \(m\)-element lists that are disjoint at distinct nonadjacent vertices. A clique-partition assignment gives a common list to the vertices of each part of a clique partition and uses disjoint lists on different parts. In this paper, we construct a graph on \(20\) vertices for which these assignments do not attain \(f'(G,20)\), and a fixed graph on \(25\) vertices for which they fail to attain the minimum for every allowed list size. For every triangle-free graph \(G\) on \(n\ge2\) vertices, we prove \[ f'(G,m)=\binom{m}{2}^{ν(G)}m^{n-2ν(G)} \qquad (m\ge n), \] where \(ν(G)\) is the size of a maximum matching, and characterize all minimizing assignments in terms of maximum matchings. For clique blow-ups of each fixed odd cycle of length at least five, we determine the minimum up to constant factors uniformly over the blow-up size and all allowed list sizes, and obtain an exponential separation from the clique-partition value. We also prove that a noncomplete graph \(G\) satisfies \(f'(G,n)=n^2\) if and only if all edges of its complement have a common endpoint. These results disprove the general clique-partition conjecture of Gravier, Maffray, and Mohar (\emph{Discrete Mathematics}, 2003) and its extension by Wu and Zhang (\emph{Applied Mathematics Letters}, 2006), while establishing both triangle-free conjectures.

items.title: Towards a twistless converse theorem
items.summary: We prove a finiteness theorem for Dirichlet series satisfying the Euler product, analytic continuation, and functional equation expected of a holomorphic newform. For any fixed level $N$, even weight $k$, and exponent $σ$, only finitely many such series have Dirichlet coefficients $\ll n^σ$. No hypotheses on twists by Dirichlet characters are assumed. The proof combines a combinatorial spanning theorem for Ramanujan sums with an operator-theoretic argument that uses two distinct primes to establish discreteness of the possible Hecke eigenvalues.

items.title: Large time behavior of global solutions to one-dimensional non-isentropic compressible Navier-Stokes-Poisson equations with large initial data
items.summary: In this paper, we are concerned with the construction of global solutions to the Cauchy problem for the one-dimensional non-isentropic compressible Navier-Stokes-Poisson equations, as well as the precise description of their large-time behavior. While results for small initial data are well-established, the case of large initial perturbations remains less satisfactory. Even for constant transport coefficients, only the Nishida-Smoller type solutions have been obtained so far. In this work, we will provide a complete resolution of this problem. The key idea involves revealing favorable hidden identities of the potential force and a new representation for the specific volume, which enables us to derive uniform upper and lower bounds on this quantity. Moreover, this strategy extends to compressible viscous single-ion flow under the Boltzmann relation; notably, this new method for deriving lower and upper bounds on the specific volume also applies to the Navier-Stokes equations. The proof relies on a domain decomposition technique and some new dissipative structures to close the nonlinear energy estimates.

items.title: On minimal singular vectors of $V^κ(\mathfrak{g})$ for types $B$ and $C$
items.summary: Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a finite-dimensional simple Lie algebra of type $B$ or $C$ over ${\mathbb C}$. Given $κ\in{\mathbb C}$, let $V^κ(\mathfrak{g})$ be the universal affine vertex algebra associated with $\mathfrak{g}$ at level $κ$. We characterize the weights of minimal singular vectors of $V^κ(\mathfrak{g})$ with respect to the generalized Cartan matrix, when $V^κ(\mathfrak{g})$ is not simple and $κ$ is not critical. Furthermore, we determine the corresponding longest Weyl elements in the Kashiwara-Tanisaki character theorem of the singular vectors.

items.title: Free $T_n$-Heyting algebras
items.summary: ${T}_n$-Heyting algebras form a subvariety of Heyting algebras and are characterized by the property that a chain of prime filters in such an algebra has at most $n-1$ elements. We study some basic properties of these algebras and determine the structure and number of elements of the free ${T}_n$-Heyting algebra with a finite number $r$ of free generators, $FT_n(r)$.

items.title: Foliated and Mather-Jacobian discrepancies via tangential arcs
items.summary: We express the log discrepancies of co-rank one foliations on normal varieties in terms of arc codimensions and differential orders. On smooth threefolds, if a foliation has simple singularities and its separatrices form an algebraic simple normal crossings divisor, we identify its foliated discrepancies with those of an ordinary pair for every divisor centred on the separatrices. This gives adjunction and log canonical threshold formulae. For algebraic images of the separatrices, we estimate changes in boundary orders caused by failure of ideal generation and by descent through the conductor. For locally complete intersection images, comparison on a common resolution yields criteria for equality of discrepancies and bounds on log canonical thresholds.

items.title: The parity of the number of missing integers in partitions
items.summary: Missing integers in partitions have been studied by many authors. A missing integer of a partition is a positive integer smaller than its largest part that does not occur as a part. We investigate parity biases for the number of missing integers in partitions and overpartitions. For every integer $c\ge2$, we prove that the coefficients $a_c(n)$ of $(-cq;q)_\infty/(-q;q)_\infty$ are eventually strictly positive and provide an effectively computable threshold. The proof uses the circle method, combining a saddle-point analysis on the major arc with explicit uniform estimates on the minor arcs. Specializing to $c=2$ and $c=3$, and verifying the remaining finite cases, we show that partitions and overpartitions of $n$ with an even number of missing integers outnumber those with an odd number for $n>34$ and $n>27$, respectively. We further prove that, for $n>10$, the difference between the numbers of ordinary partitions with an even and an odd number of missing integers is smaller than the number of partitions of $n$ into distinct parts. These results confirm three conjectures of Bhoria, Eyyunni and Santra. We also give a combinatorial interpretation of $a_c(n)$ for every integer $c\ge4$ in terms of colored partitions, generalizing the partition and overpartition interpretations of Bhoria, Eyyunni and Santra for $c=2$ and $c=3$, respectively.

items.title: Log-concavity and level set curvature estimates for the first Dirichlet eigenfunction in hyperbolic space
items.summary: In this paper, we study the first Dirichlet eigenfunction on bounded, smooth and strictly horo-convex domains in hyperbolic space $\mathbb{H}^n$. We prove its strict $\log$-concavity in arbitrary dimension and establish the Gauss curvature bound $K>1$ for its level sets. In dimensions two and three, we further obtain quantitative lower bounds for $K$ in terms of the minimum Gauss curvature of the boundary. In higher dimensions, the product of the two smallest principal curvatures of each level hypersurface exceeds one. Furthermore, we extend the strict $\log$-concavity result to bounded smooth horo-convex domains. Our approach combines maximum or minimum principles for suitable auxiliary functions, boundary convexity estimates and a domain deformation argument.

items.title: Global Solvability in Critical Sobolev Spaces for divergence-type equations associated with elliptic systems of vector fields
items.summary: In this work, we present global solvability results, in critical Sobolev spaces, for divergence-type equations associated with elliptic systems of vector fields.

items.title: Construction of Transverse Metrics from Transversely Elliptic Operators on Foliated Manifolds
items.summary: The existence of a transverse metric on a foliated manifold is typically used as a framework for studying transversely elliptic basic differential operators. This article details a method for constructing such a transverse metric directly from the principal symbol of the operator. Consequently, rather than treating the transverse metric as a mere working assumption, we demonstrate that its existence is a necessary condition for the very presence of a transversely elliptic operator.

items.title: XM4D: 4D Reconstruction through Certifiable Geometric Optimization
items.summary: Accurate 4D reconstruction remains challenging: jointly estimating camera motion, scene geometry, and non-rigid deformation entails highly nonconvex optimization, making global optimality difficult to guarantee. We present XM4D, a framework for accurate and efficient 4D reconstruction built upon certifiably globally optimal geometric optimization. By separating the estimation of camera motion from non-rigid deformation, we formulate both stages as structured quadratically constrained quadratic programs (QCQP) that admit semidefinite programming (SDP) relaxations and verifiable global optimality certificates. For camera motion estimation, we lift static point tracks into 3D using foundational depth prediction models and formulate a scaled bundle adjustment problem that jointly estimates camera poses, depth scales, and static landmarks. By analytically eliminating translations and landmarks, we reduce the problem to a QCQP over scaled rotations. For non-rigid reconstruction, we represent dynamic motion using an embedded deformation graph (EDG) and show that its tracking, rigidity, and temporal regularization objectives similarly reduce to a rotation-only QCQP. Both problems admit SDP relaxations that we solve efficiently with a GPU-accelerated Burer-Monteiro solver based on Riemannian optimization. The recovered geometry further initializes dynamic Gaussian splatting for photometric refinement. Extensive experiments across seven benchmarks demonstrate accurate camera motion estimation on both static and dynamic scenes, efficient optimization that scales to thousands of frames, and state-of-the-art novel-view rendering quality.

items.title: Topological classification of Bazaikin spaces
items.summary: In this paper, we establish a topological classification of Bazaikin spaces whose sixth cohomology groups have orders prime to \(5\). Moreover, we obtain an estimate for the number of diffeomorphism types among these spaces.

items.title: Pointwise convergence of noncommutative discrete spherical ergodic averages
items.summary: In this paper, we establish spherical maximal inequalities associated with commuting trace-preserving automorphisms on von Neumann algebras, extending Magyar-Stein-Wainger's discrete spherical maximal inequalities to the noncommutative setting. On a noncommutative probability space, we further prove that, under a strong ergodicity assumption, the corresponding discrete spherical averages converge bilaterally almost uniformly to $τ(x)1$ for every $x\in L_p(\mathcal M)$, $\frac{d}{d-2}<p\leq\infty$, when $d\geq5$.

items.title: A non-trivial index difference on surfaces of genus at least $3$
items.summary: For every closed surface of genus at least $3$, equipped with any bounding spin structure, we show that the index difference, viewed as a map from the fundamental group of the space of Dirac-invertible Riemannian metrics to $\KO^{-4}(*)$, is non-trivial. If the genus is at least $5$, we also show that the aforementioned index difference is surjective. For products of two closed surfaces of genus at least $3$, equipped with any spin structure, we prove that the corresponding space of Dirac-invertible Riemannian metrics is not contractible. We discuss the relationship of this result to the existence of metrics with harmonic spinors in dimension~$4$.

items.title: The second reconstruction transition for random graphs from 2-neighborhoods
items.summary: We prove that, with high probability, the Erdős--Rényi random graph $G(n,p)$ is reconstructible up to isomorphism from the multiset of its rooted induced 2-neighborhoods whenever $p\geq n^{-3/4}(\log n)^3$. Together with the non-reconstructibility result of Johnston, Kronenberg, Roberts and Scott, our result locates the second reconstruction transition at the scale $p=n^{-3/4}$ up to polylogarithmic factors, resolving a question they posed. Our proof relies on a global rigidity argument exploiting 5-cycle constraints.

items.title: Group-free radial Kunze-Stein phenomenon on affine buildings
items.summary: We give a geometric proof of the radial Kunze--Stein phenomenon on the good vertices of a thick, locally finite, regular affine building of irreducible type. The proof uses a positive spherical function, its joint eigenvalues for sphere averages, and the growth of vector-distance spheres. Conjugation by this function and complex interpolation yield a weighted $\ell^2$ estimate and the boundedness of radial operators with $\ell^p$ kernels for $1\leq p<2$. We also present proofs by the averaging operators norms, by the Schur test and by Helgason transform. A further interpolation gives weighted mixed-exponent estimates. No transitivity assumption on the automorphism group is required; in particular the argument applies to buildings of type $\widetilde A_2$ without a Bruhat--Tits realization.

items.title: A secondary index map on relative K-homology
items.summary: We introduce a secondary index map from relative K-homology to the K-theory of a relative structure algebra. We prove an algebraic Mayer-Vietoris sequence for the relative structure algebra, and prove compatibility of the secondary index map with the Mayer-Vietoris boundary map. As an application, we compute the secondary index of the Dirac operator on an even-dimensional spin manifold with collared metric having uniformly positive scalar curvature on the boundary. This computation leads to a refinement of the delocalized APS-index theorem.

items.title: Scaling Symmetries and Conformal Relative Equilibria on Poisson Manifolds, with Applications to Lie-Poisson Systems
items.summary: We investigate conformal relative equilibria for Hamiltonian systems on exact Poisson manifolds equipped with scaling symmetries. By introducing conformally Poisson actions and conformal momentum maps, we characterize these equilibria through an augmented Hamiltonian formulation; in the nondegenerate case, this recovers the conditions recently developed for the exact symplectic case. Specializing to the Lie-Poisson manifold $\mathfrak g^*$ associated with an arbitrary finite-dimensional real Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$, we show that its natural scaling action makes $\mathfrak g^*$ an exact Poisson manifold. We then establish a purely algebraic existence criterion: there exists a homogeneous Hamiltonian on $\mathfrak g^*$ admitting a nontrivial conformal relative equilibrium if and only if $\mathfrak g$ contains an element whose adjoint operator has a nonzero real eigenvalue. Applying this criterion to the Bianchi classification, we identify exactly the real three-dimensional Lie algebras for which there exists a homogeneous Hamiltonian admitting a nontrivial conformal relative equilibrium. As a prominent application, we show that nontrivial conformal relative equilibria exist for a rigid body on $\mathfrak{so}(2,1)^*$, whereas the classical free rigid body on $\mathfrak{so}(3)^*$ admits no nontrivial conformal relative equilibria.

items.title: The minimal excludant and the least $r$-gaps of $\ell$-regular partitions
items.summary: The minimal excludant (mex) of an integer partition $λ$ is the smallest positive integer that is not a part of $λ$. In this paper we study an analogue of this statistic for $\ell$-regular partitions with $\ell\geq2$, that is, partitions in which no part is divisible by $\ell$. Recently, Meher \cite{Meher} defined the minimal excludant for $\ell$-regular partitions. Motivated by Meher \cite{Meher}, for an $\ell$-regular partition we define its least $r$-gap as the smallest positive integer not divisible by $\ell$ that appears fewer than $r$ times as a part, and we obtain the two-variable generating function for the number of $\ell$-regular partitions of $n$ with a given least $r$-gap. Let $σ^{\mex}_{\ell}(n)$, and $σ^{\mex}_{\ell,r}(n)$ be the sum of the of the mex values over all $\ell$-regular partitions of $n$ and least $r$-gaps over all $\ell$-regular partitions of $n$ respectively. Using Jacobi's triple product identity, we derive explicit expressions for the generating function of $σ^{\mex}_{\ell}(n)$, and $σ^{\mex}_{\ell,r}(n)$, with separate formulas for even and odd $\ell$. We also show that the sequence $\{σ^{\mex}_{\ell,r}(n)\}_{n\ge0}$ is weakly increasing for every $\ell\ge2$ and $r\ge1$. Also, using Ingham's Tauberian theorem, we establish Hardy--Ramanujan type asymptotic formulas for $σ^{\mex}_{\ell,r}(n)$ when $\ell=4,5,7$ and $r\ge1$ is arbitrary. Lastly, we prove $σ^{\mex}_{\ell,r}$ is odd infinitely often, and we establish a quantitative lower bound, showing that the number of such n up to X grows at least like log log X.

items.title: A Feynman-Kac Representation and Large Deviation Bounds for the Fisher-KPP Equation Driven by Finite-Activity Pure Jump Noise
items.summary: We study the asymptotic propagation speed of travelling wave solutions to the stochastic Fisher-KPP equation with multiplicative finite-activity pure jump Lévy noise. The noise is represented by a compensated Poisson random measure with finite intensity, so that the solution evolves deterministically between successive jump times and undergoes multiplicative jumps at the event times. Our main contribution is a stochastic Feynman-Kac representation for the solution, which expresses the random field as the product of the exponential martingale of the jump noise and an expectation over the paths of an independent Brownian motion. This representation is the key probabilistic tool that converts the nonlinear stochastic partial differential equation into an expectation problem, thereby allowing for a direct analysis of the front position. Building on this representation and on the large deviation analysis of the jump noise, we derive explicit upper and lower bounds for the asymptotic wave speed. These bounds are given in terms of the noise intensity $ε$ and the Lévy measure $μ$, providing a quantitative description of how discontinuous stochastic forcing affects the propagation speed in the Fisher-KPP equation. Under the finite-activity assumption, a stopping-time iteration yields pathwise $L^\infty$ bounds and finite-speed propagation of the level sets of the front, which are essential for establishing the existence of a travelling wave profile. The framework extends naturally to multi-species cooperative systems, illustrating its robustness. Numerical simulations are included to demonstrate the informativeness of the theoretical speed bounds.

items.title: Local and 2-Local Derivations of Finite-Dimensional Zinbiel Algebras
items.summary: We study local and $2$-local derivations of finite-dimensional Zinbiel algebras. Over any field of characteristic zero, every Zinbiel algebra $A$ with $A^2 \neq 0$ and $\dim A \leq 4$ admits a proper local derivation. The proof uses a filtration argument. We exhibit two five-dimensional Zinbiel algebras with nonzero multiplication whose derivations are all central. Every local derivation on either algebra is therefore a derivation, so the minimum dimension for local rigidity with nonzero multiplication is five. Annihilator-valued interpolation gives a general construction of proper local derivations. When $A^3 = 0$, the multiplication tensor describes all derivations and local derivations. For a finite-dimensional nilpotent algebra $A$ over any field, we show that every $2$-local derivation is a derivation if and only if $\dim(A/A^2) \leq 1$. The proof combines the annihilator interpolation of Sh. Ayupov, K. Kudaybergenov and B. Omirov with a one-generator argument. When all derivations are central, every $2$-local derivation is obtained by composing a homogeneous map $A/A^2 \to \text{Ann}(A)$ with the quotient map, and every such composition is a $2$-local derivation. The five-dimensional examples extend to locally rigid Zinbiel algebras with nonlinear $2$-local derivations in every dimension at least five. We also show that derivations given by left multiplication form a Lie ideal of nilpotency class at most two and give sufficient conditions for the existence of left outer derivations. This ideal is zero in our locally rigid examples.

items.title: Massless Representations in Conformal Space and Their de Sitter Restrictions
items.summary: The monograph offers a coherent and self-contained treatment of massless (ladder) representations of the conformal group U(2,2) and their restriction to the de Sitter group Sp(2,2), combining rigorous representation-theoretic analysis with fully explicit constructions. It systematically develops these representations, including the derivation of invariant bilinear forms and Casimir operators, and constructs vertex operators and two-point functions for low-helicity fields. A central and distinctive contribution is the introduction of a canonical Clifford-split-octonion framework, in which 8-component Majorana spinors are realized within an alternative composition algebra, providing a unified and intrinsically defined setting for the algebraic, spinorial, and geometric structures underlying the theory. By bridging abstract symmetry principles with concrete computational methods and physically motivated applications in quantum field theory and cosmology, the monograph advances both conceptual clarity and technical control. While primarily addressed to researchers in mathematical physics and related fields, the exposition is carefully structured to guide advanced graduate students through subtle constructions, maintaining accessibility without compromising mathematical precision.

items.title: Extending graph metrics to hyperspaces of vertex sets: optimization and reinforcement learning applications
items.summary: An undirected connected graph can be interpreted as a metric space by considering the path distance between its vertices. Extending this perspective, we explore how walks in the graph, viewed as sequences of subsets of vertices $V$, fit into a more general framework where the path distance emerges as a special case of broader metrics that define hypertopologies on the space of subsets of $V$. In this paper, we propose a general framework to address this issue, motivated by the extension of recent reinforcement learning algorithms on graphs through Lipschitz function extensions. Our approach demonstrates how models for dynamical systems and related machine learning techniques can be adapted to (quasi-pseudo-metric) hyperspaces, offering a novel perspective for the analysis and modeling of dynamical systems. Finally, we illustrate the practical relevance of our theoretical contributions through a concrete graph optimization example, highlighting the utility and effectiveness of our proposed approach.

items.title: Liouville systems I: Blow-up analysis and orthogonal decomposition
items.summary: We study blow-up solutions of generalized Liouville systems on a closed surface at and near critical parameter hypersurfaces. Under a Morse assumption on the reduced functional, we establish the following results. First, we introduce amplitude variables in the approximate manifold and prove that every sequence of blow-up solutions at a fixed critical parameter, or along an admissible sequence from the lower side, admits a unique minimizing decomposition up to permutation. The remainder converges to zero and is orthogonal to the center, scale, and amplitude directions. The concentration scales are comparable, the limiting configuration satisfies the scale balance conditions, and the amplitudes vanish after multiplication by the logarithmic scale. Second, we determine the leading parameter defect in both critical decay regimes and prove that, along each fixed admissible path, all sufficiently large solutions lie in finitely many disjoint bubbling neighborhoods. Finally, assuming the leading coefficient is nonzero at every balanced critical configuration, the solution set at the fixed critical parameter is compact. These results provide the analytic foundation for studying the resonant degree via critical points at infinity.

items.title: Three-critical hypergraphs of maximum local edge connectivity two
items.summary: For a hypergraph \(G\), let \(χ(G)\) denote its chromatic number and \(λ(G)\) the maximum, over pairs of distinct vertices, of the minimum size of an edge cut separating the pair. A hypergraph is \(3\)-critical if its chromatic number is three and every proper subhypergraph is two-colorable. In this paper, we give a recursive characterization of the \(3\)-critical hypergraphs with \(λ(G)\le2\). We prove that these are precisely the hypergraphs generated from ordinary odd cycles and an explicit family of labeled-tree hypergraphs by admissible Toft splits. This characterization includes a necessary and sufficient condition for a prescribed split to preserve \(λ\le2\). The condition involves only cuts in the first factor and the two traces on the split edge. More generally, we establish an exact cut formula for splits at degree-\(k\) vertices of \((k+1)\)-critical hypergraphs, for every \(k\ge2\). We further prove that the smallest member of this critical class outside the family generated by hyperwheels and both forms of the Hajós join has eight vertices and is unique up to isomorphism. Together, these results resolve two issues left open by Schweser, Stiebitz, and Toft in \emph{Journal of Combinatorics} (2022): the characterization of hypergraphs with \(λ(G)=2\) and \(χ(G)=3\), and whether hyperwheels and Hajós joins suffice to generate all \(3\)-critical hypergraphs in this connectivity range.

items.title: Existence and multiplicity of $L^2$-Normalized solutions for the periodic Schrödinger system of Hamiltonian type
items.summary: In this paper, we study the following nonlinear Schrödinger system of Hamiltonian type \begin{equation*} \left\{\begin{array}{l} -Δu+V(x)u=\partial_v H(x,u,v)+ωv,\ x \in \mathbb{R}^N, \\ -Δv+V(x)v=\partial_u H(x,u,v)+ωu,\ x \in \mathbb{R}^N, \\ \displaystyle\int_{\R^N}|z|^2dx=a^2, \end{array}\right. \end{equation*} where the potential function $V(x)$ is periodic, $z:=(u,v):\R^N\rightarrow \R\times\R$, $ω\in \R$ appears as a Lagrange multiplier, $a>0$ is a prescribed constant. The existence and multiplicity of $L^2$-normalized solutions for the above Schrödinger system are obtained. The proof combines a constrained variational reduction, compactness estimates, and a Ljusternik--Schnirelmann type multiplicity theorem. In addition, a bifurcation result is also given.

items.title: A Hypergeometric RM Surface: Integral Monodromy and Level-11 Covers
items.summary: We study a genus-two hypergeometric family whose Jacobians have real multiplication by $\Q(\sqrt5)$. We identify the relevant primitive factor and integral rank-two monodromy; at one real embedding the projective image is $Δ(2,5,\infty)$, while the conjugate image is nondiscrete. At the primes above $11$, the degree-$12$ Borel covers are quadratic pullbacks of genus-one triangular modular curves. The same rank-two systems have finite-field hypergeometric Frobenius traces, yielding the local Euler factors and a quadratic transformation twisted by the character of $2$.

items.title: Log canonical singularities of plurisubharmonic functions
items.summary: A plurisubharmonic weight is \emph{log canonical} if it is at the critical point of turning non-integrable. Given a log canonical plurisubharmonic weight, we show that locally there always exists a log canonical `holomorphic' weight having the same non-integrable locus. The proof uses the theory of quasimonomial valuations developed by Jonsson-Mustaţă and Xu, as well as the minimal model program over complex analytic spaces due to Fujino and Lyu-Murayama. As a consequence, we obtain that the non-integrable locus is seminormal.

items.title: Graph-theoretic framework for semi-Markov networks: transient and stationary occupation probabilities, hitting times and weak ergodicity breaking
items.summary: We show that finite semi-Markov networks admit explicit combinatorial representations of their Laplace-transformed occupation probabilities and hitting-time distributions as sums over weighted spanning trees and forests of an augmented graph, generalizing the previously developed graph-theoretic framework for Markov networks. These representations yield asymptotic results, including the long-time scaling of hitting-time survival probabilities in the presence of infinite-mean sojourn times. They also extend recently derived combinatorial formulas for hitting-time moments to the semi-Markov setting, where non-Markovian corrections appear in higher moments. For finite-mean sojourn times, the framework recovers the known stationary distribution through a generalization of the Markov Chain Tree Theorem, with transition rates replaced by pseudo-rates. In particular, the mean hitting-time formula coincides with that of a Markov network with the corresponding pseudo-rates, which also yields a short graph-theoretic proof of the previously established constancy of Kemeny's constant for finite-mean semi-Markov networks. Finally, we use the same framework to extend established results on weak ergodicity breaking for time-additive state observables that are nonconstant on the support of the limiting distribution in heavy-tailed semi-Markov networks, allowing for generally heterogeneous, transition-dependent waiting-time distributions.
